lore: Frank Holiday is a supporting character in the games Detective Pikachu and Detective Pikachu Returns . He is a police inspector in Ryme City .

title: Brad McMaster
lore: Brad McMaster is a reoccurring character in the games Detective Pikachu and Detective Pikachu Returns . He is a lieutenant in the Ryme City Police Department.

title: Ethan Graham
lore: Ethan Graham is a character in the game Detective Pikachu .

title: Roger Clifford
lore: Roger Clifford (Japanese: ロジャー・クリフォード  Roger Clifford ) is the main antagonist of Detective Pikachu and a supporting character of the film adaptation . In the movie, he is portrayed by Chris Geere .

title: Kazumasa Iwao
lore: Kazumasa Iwao (Japanese: 岩尾和昌  Iwao Kazumasa ) is a game designer and director who has worked at Game Freak since 2008. [ 1 ] He has been involved with main series Pokémon games as a game designer since Pokémon Black and White Versions . He was appointed by Shigeru Ohmori as the director for Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon . He also appeared in the form of an NPC as Iwao (Japanese: イワオ ) in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon .

title: Necrozma (game)
lore: Necrozma (Japanese: ネクロズマ  Necrozma ), also referred to as the Blinding One (Japanese: かがやきさま  Radiant One ) by the Ultra Recon Squad , and known as the pillager of light (Japanese: 光 ( ひかり ) の 略奪者 ( りゃくだつしゃ )  pillager of light ) in Alola mythology, is a major antagonist in Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon . it serves as one of the main threats in the game, looking to take the light of the Alola region in order to regain its original form and power.

title: Soliera
lore: Soliera (Japanese: ミリン  Mirin ) is a member of the Ultra Recon Squad . She and Phyco play a central role in Pokémon Ultra Moon .

title: Phyco
lore: Phyco (Japanese: シオニラ  Shionira ) is the Captain of the Ultra Recon Squad . He and Soliera play a central role in Pokémon Ultra Moon .

title: Zossie
lore: Zossie (Japanese: アマモ  Amamo ) is a member of the Ultra Recon Squad . She and Dulse play a central role in Pokémon Ultra Sun .

title: Dulse
lore: Dulse (Japanese: ダルス  Dulse ) is a member of the Ultra Recon Squad . He and Zossie play a central role in Pokémon Ultra Sun .

title: Gester
lore: Gester (Japanese: ミブリ  Miburi ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon who allows the player to change their battle style . Gester appears in Malie City 's Recycling Plant on Ula'ula Island .

title: Mr. Hyper
lore: Mr. Hyper (Japanese: すごいオヤジ  Mr. Amazing ) is a character in the Generation VII  core series games that conducts Hyper Training , which maximizes one or more of a Pokémon's IVs . This process is done "through intensive training". In Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon , Mr. Hyper appears in the Hau'oli City shopping mall on Melemele Island once the player has become the Champion of the Pokémon League . In Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! , Mr. Hyper appears at the Pokémon Day Care on Route 5 after they become Champion. If given a Bottle Cap , he maximizes a single IV of a chosen Pokémon; if he is given a Gold Bottle Cap , he maximizes all of its IVs. He will only Hyper Train Pokémon that are at level 100.

title: Eevee users
lore: The Eevee users are a group of nine Trainers around Alola who use Eevee or one of its evolved forms . Each of these Trainers has a unique Trainer class based on the Pokémon they use, such as Eevee User. These Trainers constitute a challenge that the player can undertake after they become the Champion . At the Thrifty Megamart at Royal Avenue , Kagetora—a man at the leftmost cash register—will initially tell the player to visit him again once they become the strongest Trainer in Alola. When the player speaks to him after becoming the Champion, he will explain that he's looking for a capable Trainer to defeat eight Trainers he was always trying to beat 30 years ago: the other Eevee users. He promises to reward the player if they can manage this feat. Prior to speaking to Kagetora, the player will not be able to find any of the other Eevee users anywhere. They only appear once the player is tasked with finding them.

title: Harper and Sarah
lore: Harper (Japanese: ホウ  Hō ) and Sarah (Japanese: スイ  Sui ) are characters appearing in Pokémon Sun and Moon and Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon , as well as in Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon . They are the younger twin sisters of Lana .

title: Samson Oak
lore: Samson Oak (Japanese: ナリヤ・オーキド  Nariya Ohkido ) is a Pokémon Professor in Alola . He studies the regional forms and Totem Pokémon of the region . He is a cousin of Professor Oak , with whom he shares a striking resemblance.

title: Mom (Alola)
lore: Mom (Japanese: おかあさん  mother ) is the mother of the player in Pokémon Sun and Moon and Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon .

title: Mohn
lore: Mohn (Japanese: モーン  Mohn ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is Lillie and Gladion 's father, Lusamine 's husband, and a former Aether Foundation researcher.

title: Lusamine
lore: Lusamine (Japanese: ルザミーネ  Lusamine ) is the head of the Aether Foundation . She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Aether President (Japanese: エーテルだいひょう  Aether President ).

title: Faba
lore: Faba (Japanese: ザオボー  Sauboh ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He works at the Aether Foundation . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Aether Branch Chief (Japanese: エーテルしぶちょう  Aether Director ). He specializes in the Psychic type.

title: Wicke
lore: Wicke (Japanese: ビッケ  Wicke ) is the assistant branch chief of the Aether Foundation 's Aether Paradise .

title: Guzma
lore: Guzma (Japanese: グズマ  Guzma ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is the leader of Team Skull . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Team Skull Boss (Japanese: スカルだんボス  Team Skull Boss ). He specializes in Bug-type  Pokémon .

title: Plumeria
lore: Plumeria (Japanese: プルメリ  Plumeri ) is the Admin of Team Skull . She is considered the "big sister" of the team, due to how she runs operations strictly but also cares for her underlings. She specializes in Poison-type  Pokémon . She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Team Skull Admin (Japanese: スカルだんかんぶ  Team Skull Executive ).

title: Gladion
lore: Gladion (Japanese: グラジオ  Glazio ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He works for Team Skull as an enforcer, and serves as a rival character to the player in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Team Skull (Japanese: スカルだん  Skull Gang ).

title: Ryuki
lore: Ryuki (Japanese: リュウキ  Ryūki ) is a non-player character in the Generation VII  games . He is a rock guitarist and a Pokémon Trainer who specializes in Dragon-type  Pokémon .

title: Molayne
lore: Molayne (Japanese: マーレイン  Mullein ) is a non-player character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is a Pokémon Trainer who specializes in Steel-type  Pokémon . Sophocles affectionately refers to him as Big Mo (Japanese: マーさん  Mu-san ). He also becomes a member of the Alola  Elite Four in Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon .

title: Kahili
lore: Kahili (Japanese: カヒリ  Kahili ) is a Flying-type  Trainer , a previous Island Challenge Champion, and a member of the Alola  Elite Four .

title: Hapu
lore: Hapu (Japanese: ハプウ  Hapu'u ) is the island kahuna of Poni Island . She specializes in Ground-type  Pokémon . She grants the Poni stamp to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Nanu
lore: Nanu (Japanese: クチナシ  Kuchinashi )  is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is the kahuna of Ula'ula Island . He specializes in Dark-type  Pokémon . He grants the Ula'ula stamp to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Olivia
lore: Olivia (Japanese: ライチ  Lychee )  is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . She is the kahuna of Akala Island and a member of the Alola  Elite Four . She specializes in Rock-type  Pokémon . She grants the Akala Trial Completion stamp to Trainers who defeat her in a grand trial.

title: Hala
lore: Hala (Japanese: ハラ  Hala )  is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is the grandfather of Hau and the kahuna of Melemele Island . He specializes in Fighting-type  Pokémon and grants the Melemele stamp to Trainers who defeat him. In Sun and Moon, he also becomes a member of the Alola  Elite Four .

title: Mina
lore: Mina (Japanese: マツリカ  Matsurika ) is the captain of Poni Island , her primary trial grounds being her house in Seafolk Village . She specializes in Fairy-type  Pokémon .

title: Acerola
lore: Acerola (Japanese: アセロラ  Acerola ) is the captain of Thrifty Megamart's abandoned site on Ula'ula Island . She is also a Ghost-type  Trainer and a member of the Alola  Elite Four .

title: Sophocles
lore: Sophocles (Japanese: マーマネ  Mamane ) is the captain of Ula'ula Island 's Hokulani Observatory . He specializes in Electric-type  Pokémon . Molayne affectionately refers to him as Soffy (Japanese: マーくん  Mā-kun ).

title: Mallow
lore: Mallow (Japanese: マオ  Mao ) is one of the captains of Akala Island whose trial takes place at Lush Jungle . She specializes in Grass-type  Pokémon .

title: Kiawe
lore: Kiawe (Japanese: カキ  Kaki ) is the captain of Akala Island 's Wela Volcano Park . He specializes in Fire-type  Pokémon .

title: Lana
lore: Lana (Japanese: スイレン  Suiren ) is the captain of Akala Island 's Brooklet Hill . She is described as an expert with Water-type  Pokémon who is dedicated to her family and a reliable older sister who watches over her younger sisters.

title: Ilima
lore: Ilima (Japanese: イリマ  Ilima ) is the captain of Melemele Island 's Verdant Cavern . He specializes in Normal-type  Pokémon .

title: Rotom Pokédex
lore: The Rotom Pokédex (Japanese: ロトム 図鑑 ( ずかん )  Rotom illustrated encyclopedia ), referred to as Rotom Dex in-game, is an electronic device and character found in the Alola  region that appears in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . The Pokémon character inside, simply known by its species name as Rotom (Japanese: ロトム  Rotom ), can enhance the Pokédex by possessing the device as it would with other electronics. This special Pokédex is said to be rare, even in Alola. While inside the Pokédex, Rotom can speak with the player or other characters. It is given to the player by Professor Kukui . In addition to functioning as a regular Pokédex, the Rotom Pokédex also has other features, such as a map and the ability to call people to and from other locations.

title: Professor Kukui
lore: Professor Kukui (Japanese: ククイ博士  Dr. Kukui ) is a Pokémon Professor from the Alola region, as well as the founder of Alola's Pokémon League . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Pro Wrestler (Japanese: プロレスラー  Pro Wrestler ) under the alias the Masked Royal (Japanese: ロイヤルマスク  Royal Mask ). He specializes in Pokémon moves .

title: Hau
lore: Hau (Japanese: ハウ  Hau ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . He is the grandson of the island kahuna for Melemele Island , Hala . He serves as one of the player's friends and rivals in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon .

title: Nebby
lore: Nebby (Japanese: ほしぐもちゃん  Hoshigumo-chan )  is a Solgaleo S US / Lunala M UM , a Legendary  Pokémon , and a major character in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . Its nickname was given to it as a Cosmog by Lillie , who took care of it and tried to uncover its mysteries.

title: Lillie
lore: Lillie (Japanese: リーリエ  Lilie ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Sun and Moon . In Pokémon Sun, Moon, Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon , she serves as one of the player character 's friends and traveling companions during the course of the game. In Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, she eventually becomes a Pokémon Trainer , specializing in Fairy-type  Pokémon .

title: Selene (game)
lore: Selene (Japanese: ミヅキ  Mizuki ) is the female player character in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . Her male counterpart is Elio .

title: Elio (game)
lore: Elio (Japanese: ヨウ  Yō ) is the male player character in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . His female counterpart is Selene .

title: Mateo
lore: Mateo (Japanese: マテオ  Mateo ) is a character in Pokémon GO . He is a researcher who loves to travel, as well as collecting and exchanging Gifts and Postcards . He provides the Gift Exchange service for players exploring Routes .

title: Rhi
lore: Rhi (Japanese: リイ  Rhi ) is a member of the GO Ultra Recon Squad . They debuted on Pokémon GO Fest 2022 Day 2 as a replacement of Professor Willow . They specialize in learning about Pokémon that arrive from Ultra Space .

title: Arlo
lore: Arlo (Japanese: アルロ  Arlo ) is one of the Leaders of Team GO Rocket in Pokémon GO . Arlo is known to be sly and manipulative. After losing to Candela for the position of Team Valor Leader, Arlo joined Team GO Rocket, where he has contributed greatly to its Shadow Pokémon program. [ 1 ]

title: Cliff (GO)
lore: Cliff (Japanese: クリフ  Cliff ) is one of the Leaders of Team GO Rocket in Pokémon GO . He has a short temper, and he is feared for his strength and his intolerance to disloyalty. However, he's also renowned at the same time for his big heart and kind soul. [ 1 ]  Multiple of Cliff's in-game quotes note his loyalty to Team GO Rocket, with him stating that he "owes the boss [his] life" and that "Team GO Rocket saved [him]". [ 2 ]  Starting June 10, 2023, Cliff began appearing at Gyms, taking them over in five-star Shadow Raids using Shadow Articuno . Defeating him allowed players to capture Shadow Articuno in the bonus challenge, with a possibility of it being Shiny.

title: Sierra
lore: Sierra (Japanese: シエラ  Sierra ) is one of the Leaders of Team GO Rocket in Pokémon GO . A street-smart loner, she has grown up under difficult circumstances, allowing her to learn martial arts. As she rose within the ranks of Team GO Rocket, she became Giovanni 's most trusted confidant. [ 1 ]

title: Blanche
lore: Blanche (Japanese: ブランシェ  Blanche ) is the leader of Team Mystic (Japanese: チームミスティック  Team Mystic ), one of the three teams in Pokémon GO . Team Mystic is researching Pokémon Evolution and is represented by Articuno . Team Mystic Trainers believe that by staying calm and analyzing every situation, they cannot lose. Blanche is one of Professor Willow 's assistants, along with Spark and Candela . Highly analytical, Blanche often loses track of time when doing research. Blanche tends to get embarrassed when proven wrong and does not take jokes well. [ 1 ] [ 2 ]

title: Spark (GO)
lore: Spark (Japanese: スパーク  Spark ) is the leader of Team Instinct (Japanese: チームインスティンクト  Team Instinct ) in Pokémon GO . Team Instinct is researching Pokémon breeding , and is represented by Zapdos . Team Instinct Trainers believe a Pokémon's intuition is linked to how they are hatched. He is one of Professor Willow 's assistants, along with Blanche and Candela . Standing at over 6 feet tall, Spark is the tallest of the three team leaders. [ 1 ] He has an impulsive personality and likes to tease Blanche, who tends to get flustered when proven wrong. [ 2 ]

title: Professor Willow
lore: Professor Willow (Japanese: ウィロー博士  Dr. Willow ) is a Pokémon Professor who appears in the Pokémon GO mobile game. Similar to Professor Birch , he specializes in Pokémon habitats and distribution. Unlike other Professors who directly give Trainers their first Pokémon, Professor Willow gives Trainers their first Poké Balls to capture their first Pokémon.

title: Karolin
lore: Karolin (Japanese: キャロル  Karol ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She organizes the Queen's Cup tournaments that take place on the S.S. Carmonte Carnival .

title: Marabelle
lore: Marabelle (Japanese: マリベル  Maribelle ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She works at Carmonte Island 's figure shop , where she takes on a managerial role.

title: Tia
lore: Tia (Japanese: ティア  Tia ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She is the younger sister of Luca , and is the primary salesperson of Carmonte Island 's figure shop .

title: Another
lore: Another (Japanese: アナザー  Another ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is Luca 's AI assistant, and his twin AI is Carlo .

title: Carlo
lore: Carlo (Japanese: カルロ  Carlo ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the player's AI assistant, and his twin AI is Another . His special move is the "Giant Miracle Smash".

title: Master Rosé
lore: Master Rosé (Japanese: マスター・ロゼ  Master Rosé ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the owner of the Jewel Tower and the Champion of the PFG World Championships, known as the "Undefeated Champion". Due to Pokémon Duel being discontinued before its story was completed, the player is never able to duel Rosé.

title: Number 7
lore: Number 7 (Japanese: ＮＯ７  NO7 ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the owner of Elysium , and one of the world's leading specialists in AI.

title: Don Roger
lore: Don Roger (Japanese: ドン・ロジャー  Don Roger ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the owner of The Volcano and the leader of the Roger family .

title: Brenda
lore: Brenda (Japanese: ブレンダ  Brenda ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She is the owner of Olivia Palace and a member of the Roger family .

title: Joe (Duel)
lore: Joe (Japanese: ジョー  Joe ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the owner of Atlantis and a member of the Roger family .

title: Nadya
lore: Nadya (Japanese: ナジャ  Nadya ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She is the owner of Château de Rosa . She also has the title of the "Multicolored Plate Spinner", due to her use of several different kinds of Plates in her battle strategies.

title: Yuji (Duel)
lore: Yuji (Japanese: ユージ  Yūji ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is the owner of Ulex .

title: Sharon (Duel)
lore: Sharon (Japanese: シャロン  Sharon ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . She is one of the player's friends and rivals . She is a famous Pokémon Figure Game (PFG) player, and is known as the "PFG Princess". Her special move is the "Red-faced Demon Blast".

title: Luca
lore: Luca (Japanese: ルカ  Luca ) is a character in Pokémon Duel . He is one of the player's friends and rivals , and the owner of an unspecified hotel. His special move is the "Luca Nova".

title: Pablo Millan
lore: Pablo Millan is a supporting character in the games Detective Pikachu and Detective Pikachu Returns . He owns and operates the Hi-Hat Café .

title: Meiko Okamoto
lore: Meiko Okamoto is a reoccurring character in the game Detective Pikachu . She is a director and camerawoman at GNN .

title: Emilia Christie
lore: Emilia Christie (Japanese: エミリア・クリスティー  Emilia Christie ) is a reoccurring character in the game Detective Pikachu . She is a rookie assistant director at GNN .

title: Amanda Blackstone
lore: Amanda Blackstone is a supporting character in the game Detective Pikachu .

title: Mike Baker
lore: Mike Baker is a supporting character in the game Detective Pikachu .

title: Harry Goodman
lore: Harry Goodman (Japanese: ハリー・グッドマン  Harry Goodman ) is the father of Tim Goodman , one of the main characters in the games Detective Pikachu and Detective Pikachu Returns , and the movie POKÉMON Detective Pikachu .

title: Detective Pikachu (character)
lore: Detective Pikachu (Japanese: 名探偵 ピカチュウ  Great Detective Pikachu ) is one of the protagonists of Detective Pikachu and the movie of the same name . He is capable of understanding human languages , but only his partner Tim Goodman can understand him.

title: Tim Goodman
lore: Tim Goodman (Japanese: ティム・グッドマン  Tim Goodman ) is the player character in the game Detective Pikachu and its sequel Detective Pikachu Returns , and one of the protagonists of the movie of the same name . He is the partner of Detective Pikachu , and the only one who can understand Pikachu's words.

title: Professor Tetra
lore: Professor Tetra (Japanese: テトラ博士  Dr. Tetra ) is a researcher and the Pokémon Professor for Pokémon Picross . She has a lab that constitutes Area 00 and teaches the player about picross puzzles. After completing Area 00, the player receives a Squirtle and Eevee from her. Daily training puzzles are offered by her.

title: Shadow Mewtwo
lore: Shadow Mewtwo (Japanese: ダークミュウツー  Dark Mewtwo ) is an unlockable Battle Pokémon in the fighting game Pokkén Tournament . It is a Technical style fighter. Upon activating Synergy Burst, Shadow Mewtwo will Mega Evolve into Shadow Mega Mewtwo X.

title: Nia (Pokkén)
lore: Nia (Japanese: ニア  Nia ) is an advisor and battle trainer that assists players in Pokkén Tournament .

title: Amelia
lore: Amelia (Japanese: アミリア  Amelia ) is a character in Pokémon Shuffle . She works as a journalist. She acts as the tutorial for the game, tagging along with the player as they explore Puerto Blanco and explaining the mechanics. After the first stage of Sandy Bazaar , she says goodbye as she leaves to write a report based on the player's journey . She briefly returns after the player enters Night Festival with a small gift. Her recommendation icons start to appear next to the Pokemon that the player can catch in the game's menus. Each Pokémon has zero to five icons, and the more icons it has the more Amelia recommends the player to use that Pokémon. This loosely corresponds with the overall quality of the Pokémon. This event was added in a update, so it could happen in any zone if the player was in a different zone before downloading the update.

title: Cosplay Pikachu
lore: Cosplay Pikachu (Japanese: おきがえピカチュウ  Clothes-changing Pikachu ) is a variant female Pikachu that is able to be dressed up into five different costumes corresponding to each of the five Contest conditions ( Coolness , Beauty , Cuteness , Cleverness , and Toughness ), and learn exclusive moves , which are linked to these costumes. Without a costume, Cosplay Pikachu has the appearance of a female Pikachu with a black heart on the tip of its tail (fitting the heart-shaped notch all female Pikachu have on their tail).

title: Zinnia
lore: Zinnia (Japanese: ヒガナ  Higana ) is a mysterious Draconid woman and a Pokémon Trainer from Hoenn . She is described as a special person who holds the key to the Delta Episode in Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire , on a trip to accomplish her objectives. Zinnia uses Dragon-type  Pokémon in battle, including a Salamence she can Mega Evolve into Mega  Salamence using her Mega Anklet . She also travels with a female Whismur  nicknamed  Aster (Japanese: シガナ  Shigana ). She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Lorekeeper (Japanese: でんしょうしゃ  Lorekeeper ).

title: Aarune
lore: Aarune (Japanese: ギリー  Girī ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . He is an expert on Super-Secret Bases . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Secret Base Expert (Japanese: ひみつきちマスター  Secret Base Master ).

title: Chaz (game)
lore: Chaz (Japanese: カズラ  Kazura ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . He is a Pokémon Coordinator from Hoenn . His design is that of the Rich Boy Trainer class.

title: Lisia
lore: Lisia (Japanese: ルチア  Lutia ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . She is a Pokémon Coordinator from Sootopolis City and the niece of Wallace . For her achievements in Pokémon Contest Spectaculars , she became an idol in Hoenn , filming commercials and scouting Trainers to participate in contests.

title: Hotel Richissime
lore: Hotel Richissime (Japanese: グランドホテル シュールリッシュ  Grand Hotel Surriche ) is a large black building located on North Boulevard in Lumiose City that serves as a luxury hotel. Once a day, a man at the reception desk will let the player stay overnight, healing their Pokémon and adding 30 points of affection and 255 points of fullness in Pokémon-Amie , at the cost of $ 100,000. Malva is fought in the hotel as part of one of the missions during the Looker sidequest after upgrading the Mega Ring .

title: Phil the Photo Guy
lore: Phil the Photo Guy (Japanese: カメラおやじ  Old Man Camera ) is a non-player character in Pokémon X and Y . He takes pictures of the player at various locations in Kalos .

title: Katherine (Kalos)
lore: Katherine (Japanese: カレン  Karen ) is a Furisode Girl from the Laverre Gym . In Pokémon the Series , she is a recurring character who first appeared in A Fashionable Battle! .

title: Blossom
lore: Blossom (Japanese: シオネ  Shione ) is a recurring character who first appeared in A Fashionable Battle! .

title: Linnea
lore: Linnea (Japanese: アサミ  Asami ) is a recurring character who first appeared in A Fashionable Battle! .

title: Kali
lore: Kali (Japanese: キリカ  Kirika ) is a recurring character who first appeared in A Fashionable Battle! .

title: Mr. Bonding
lore: Mr. Bonding (Japanese: キズナおやじ  Old Man Kizuna ) is an expert on O-Powers who will give the player an O-Power every time he is encountered in Pokémon X and Y . He received the O-Powers from Hoenn 's old guys when they wanted to retire, a process which transformed him from a "powerless" man into Mr. Bonding. He appears as an adult man with dark purple hair in a light pink suit.

title: Inver
lore: Inver (Japanese: サカサ  Sakasa ) is a non-player character in the Generation VI  games . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Proprietor (Japanese: てんちょう  Proprietor ).

title: Cassius
lore: Cassius (Japanese: クロケア  Crocea ) is a computer technician that resides in Camphrier Town in Kalos .

title: Grace (Kalos)
lore: Grace (Japanese: サキ  Saki ) is the mother of the player character in Pokémon X and Y . She is an accomplished Rhyhorn racer from Vaniville Town . In Pokémon the Series , Grace is the mother of Serena and appears as a recurring character during Pokémon the Series: XY . In the Pokémon Adventures  manga , she is the mother of Y .

title: Gurkinn
lore: Gurkinn (Japanese: コンコンブル  Concombre ) is an old man introduced in Pokémon X and Y . He is the grandfather of Korrina and the descendant of the first Trainer to Mega Evolve a Pokémon.

title: Emma
lore: Emma (Japanese: マチエール  Matiere ) is a character introduced in Pokémon X and Y who plays a major role in its post-game's side story. She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer classes  Suspicious Woman (Japanese: あやしいおとな  Suspicious Adult ), Suspicious Child (Japanese: あやしいこども  Suspicious Child ), and Suspicious Lady (Japanese: あやしいおねえさん  Suspicious Miss ). In Pokémon Legends: Z-A , she inherits the head role at her detective agency from Looker in Lumiose City .

title: Dexio
lore: Dexio (Japanese: デクシオ  Dexio ) is one of Professor Sycamore 's assistants , and often appears along with another assistant, Sina . He specializes in Psychic-type  Pokémon .

title: Sina
lore: Sina (Japanese: ジーナ  Sina ) is one of Professor Sycamore 's assistants , and often appears along with another assistant, Dexio . She specializes in Ice-type  Pokémon .

title: Morgan
lore: Morgan (Japanese: ルミタン  Lematin ) is one of the four leaders of the Battle Maison in Pokémon X, Y , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , alongside her sisters Nita , Evelyn , and Dana .

title: Dana
lore: Dana (Japanese: ラジュルネ  Lajournée ) is one of the four leaders of the Battle Maison in Pokémon X, Y , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , alongside her sisters Nita , Evelyn , and Morgan .

title: Evelyn
lore: Evelyn (Japanese: ルスワール  Lesoir ) is one of the four leaders of the Battle Maison in Pokémon X, Y , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , alongside her sisters Nita , Dana , and Morgan .

title: Nita
lore: Nita (Japanese: ラニュイ  Lanuit ) is one of the four leaders of the Battle Maison in Pokémon X, Y , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , alongside her sisters Evelyn , Dana , and Morgan .

title: AZ
lore: AZ (Japanese: AZ ) is a mysterious man who appears in Pokémon X and Y and Pokémon Legends: Z-A . He is the former king of the Kalos region, the creator of the ultimate weapon , and the current owner of Hotel Z . In X and Y, he has the appearance of a disheveled homeless man, while in Legends: Z-A, he sports more formal wear. His name is pronounced as the two letters separately ("A Z").

title: Chalmers
lore: Chalmers (Japanese: アカマロ  Akamaro ) is a Butler and former Admin of Team Flare in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Mable
lore: Mable (Japanese: モミジ  Momiji ) is formerly one of five Team Flare scientists in Pokémon X and Y . She returns in Pokémon Legends: Z-A , where she is now the acting director of the Pokémon Research Lab .

title: Celosia
lore: Celosia (Japanese: コレア  Correa ) is one of five Team Flare scientists in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Bryony
lore: Bryony (Japanese: バラ  Bara ) is one of five Team Flare scientists in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Aliana
lore: Aliana (Japanese: アケビ  Akebi ) is one of five Team Flare scientists in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Lysandre
lore: Lysandre (Japanese: フラダリ  Fuladari ) is the boss of Team Flare and the main antagonist of Pokémon X and Y . He is also the owner of Lysandre Labs , the company that created the Holo Caster . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Team Flare Boss (Japanese: フレアだんボス  Team Flare Boss ). He seeks to wipe out most of the world population in order to return the planet to a beautiful, unspoiled state; what he describes as 'beautiful' is a world without 'negative' or 'ugly' concepts, such as strife, struggle, war, or despair. [ 4 ]

title: Diantha
lore: Diantha (Japanese: カルネ  Carne ) is a famous and renowned actress who is the Champion of the Kalos region's Pokémon League in Pokémon X and Y . She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Grand Duchess .

title: Wikstrom
lore: Wikstrom (Japanese: ガンピ  Gampi ) is a Steel-type  Trainer and member of the Kalos  Elite Four .

title: Siebold
lore: Siebold (Japanese: ズミ  Zumi ) is a Water-type  Trainer and member of the Kalos  Elite Four .

title: Malva
lore: Malva (Japanese: パキラ  Pachira ) is a Fire-type  Trainer and member of the Kalos  Elite Four . In addition, she was also a member of Team Flare prior to the organization's disbandment.

title: Wulfric
lore: Wulfric (Japanese: ウルップ  Urup ) is the Gym Leader of Snowbelle City 's Gym , known officially as the Snowbelle Gym . He specializes in Ice-type  Pokémon . He gives the Iceberg Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Olympia
lore: Olympia (Japanese: ゴジカ  Gojika ) is the Gym Leader of Anistar City 's Gym , known officially as the Anistar Gym . She specializes in Psychic-type  Pokémon . She gives the Psychic Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Valerie
lore: Valerie (Japanese: マーシュ  Mache ) is a fashion designer who is the Gym Leader of Laverre City 's Gym , known officially as the Laverre Gym . She specializes in Fairy-type  Pokémon . She gives the Fairy Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Clemont
lore: Clemont (Japanese: シトロン  Citron ) is an inventor who is the Gym Leader of Lumiose City 's Gym , known officially as the Lumiose Gym . He specializes in Electric-type  Pokémon . He gives the Voltage Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Ramos
lore: Ramos (Japanese: フクジ  Fukuji ) is a gardener who is the Gym Leader of Coumarine City 's Gym , known officially as the Coumarine Gym . He specializes in Grass-type  Pokémon . He gives the Plant Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Korrina
lore: Korrina (Japanese: コルニ  Corni ) is the Gym Leader of Shalour City 's Gym , known officially as the Shalour Gym . She specializes in Fighting-type  Pokémon . She gives the Rumble Badge to Trainers who defeat her. She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Successor (Japanese: けいしょうしゃ  Successor ).

title: Grant
lore: Grant (Japanese: ザクロ  Zakuro ) is an athlete who is the Gym Leader of Cyllage City 's Gym , known officially as the Cyllage Gym . He specializes in Rock-type  Pokémon . He gives the Cliff Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Viola
lore: Viola (Japanese: ビオラ  Viola ) is a professional photographer who is the Gym Leader of Santalune City 's Gym , known officially as the Santalune Gym . She specializes in Bug-type  Pokémon . She gives the Bug Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Bonnie
lore: Bonnie (Japanese: ユリーカ  Eureka ) is a young girl introduced in Pokémon X and Y . She is the younger sister of Clemont .

title: Alexa
lore: Alexa (Japanese: パンジー  Pansy ) is a journalist from Lumiose City in Pokémon X and Y . She works at the Lumiose Press .

title: Trevor
lore: Trevor (Japanese: トロバ  Trova ) is a friend and rival of the player in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Tierno
lore: Tierno (Japanese: ティエルノ  Tierno ) is a friend and rival of the player in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Shauna
lore: Shauna (Japanese: サナ  Sana ) is a friend and rival of the player in Pokémon X and Y .

title: Professor Sycamore
lore: Professor Augustine Sycamore (Japanese: プラターヌ博士  Dr. Platane ) is a Pokémon Professor from the Kalos region. He specializes in both Evolution , Mega Evolution , and change.

title: Serena (game)
lore: Serena (Japanese: セレナ  Serena ) is the female player character in Pokémon X and Y . She also serves as the rival in the same games if the player chooses to play as the male character . Her male counterpart is Calem . If playing as Serena, the player character may earn the title of Grand Duchess by defeating most of the Trainers in the Battle Chateau .

title: Calem (game)
lore: Calem (Japanese: カルム  Calme ) is the male player character in Pokémon X and Y . He serves as the rival in the same games if the player chooses to play as the female character . As a rival, he is one of the player's neighbors and close friends . His female counterpart is Serena . If playing as Calem, the player character may earn the title of Grand Duke by defeating most of the Trainers in the Battle Chateau . This is the only time the Trainer class "Grand Duke" appears in the games.

title: Professor Burnet
lore: Professor Burnet (Japanese: バーネット博士  Dr. Burnet ) is a researcher who debuted in Pokémon Dream Radar and reappears in Pokémon Sun, Moon , Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon . Her research specializes in the relationship between the Pokémon universe and other dimensions .

title: Medal (Black 2 and White 2)
lore: A Medal (Japanese: メダル  Medal ) is earned for each of several achievements in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . Medals are given by Mr. Medal in any Pokémon Center when talking to him after meeting their requirements, and are stored in the Medal Box . Mr. Medal will only appear when the player has unclaimed Medals they have achieved. There are 255 Medals in all, along with Hint Medals. They are divided into five categories: 7 Special Medals, 98 Adventure Medals, 56 Battle Medals, 75 Entertainment Medals, and 19 Challenge Medals. Medals are collected for the Medal Rally (Japanese: メダルラリー  Medal Rally ).

title: Pop Roxie
lore: Pop Roxie (Japanese: ホミカパパ  Homika's Papa ) is a character appearing in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 and the Pokémon Adventures manga.

title: Pokéstar Studios
lore: Pokéstar Studios (Japanese: ポケウッド  Pokéwood , formally called ポケウッドムービースタジオ  Pokéwood Movie Studio ) is a film studio featured in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . It is located north of Virbank City . Pokéstar Studios allows the player to take part in making films involving Pokémon. The films feature a scenario chosen by the player and a number of Pokémon battles . Pop Roxie , Brycen and Sabrina have co-starred in films produced in the studio. The facility is run by an elderly man named Stu Deeoh (Japanese: ウッドウさん  Mr. Wood ).

title: Mom (Black 2 and White 2)
lore: Mom (Japanese: おかあさん  mother ) is the mother of Nate or Rosa in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . She lives in Aspertia City , and is an old friend of Professor Juniper . She is fairly knowledgeable about the various locations in Unova, and used to work as a Pokémon Center receptionist. The Pokémon Centers she is implied to have worked in are located in Nimbasa City and Mistralton City .

title: Curtis
lore: Curtis (Japanese: テツ  Tetsu ), otherwise known under the screen name Christoph (Japanese: テンマ  Tenma ), is a character that appears in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 if the player 's gender is female. He is the male counterpart to Yancy .

title: Yancy
lore: Yancy (Japanese: ルリ  Ruri ), otherwise known under the screen name Nancy (Japanese: ルッコ  Rukko ), is a character that appears in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 if the player 's gender is male. She is the female counterpart to Curtis .

title: Benga
lore: Benga (Japanese: バンジロウ  Banjirō ) is a Pokémon Trainer from Unova . He is Alder 's grandson and the final Boss Trainer of the Black Tower B2 / White Treehollow W2 .

title: Marlon
lore: Marlon (Japanese: シズイ  Shizui ) is the Gym Leader of Humilau City 's Gym , known officially as the Humilau Gym . He specializes in Water-type  Pokémon . He gives the Wave Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Roxie
lore: Roxie (Japanese: ホミカ  Homika ) is a musician who is the Gym Leader of Virbank City 's Gym , known officially as the Virbank Gym . She specializes in Poison-type  Pokémon . She gives the Toxic Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Colress
lore: Colress (Japanese: アクロマ  Achroma ) is a Pokémon researcher and the second boss of Team Plasma , appointed by Ghetsis . His goal is to discover the true way to draw out the strength of Pokémon. He mostly specializes in Steel-type  Pokémon .

title: Hugh
lore: Hugh (Japanese: ヒュウ  Hyu ) is the rival character in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . His name is chosen by the player at the start of the game.

title: Rosa (game)
lore: Rosa (Japanese: メイ  Mei ) is the female player character in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . Her male counterpart is Nate .

title: Nate (game)
lore: Nate (Japanese: キョウヘイ  Kyouhei ) is the male player character in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . His female counterpart is Rosa .

title: Masanori
lore: Masanori (Japanese: マサノリ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . He is friends with two other Warlords, Kiyomasa and Mitsunari .

title: Kiyomasa
lore: Kiyomasa (Japanese: キヨマサ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . He is friends with two other Warlords, Mitsunari and Masanori .

title: Mitsunari
lore: Mitsunari (Japanese: ミツナリ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . He is friends with two other Warlords, Masanori and Kiyomasa .

title: Keiji
lore: Keiji (Japanese: ケイジ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Ina
lore: Ina (Japanese: イナヒメ  Inahime ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Ranmaru
lore: Ranmaru (Japanese: ランマル ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Okuni
lore: Okuni (Japanese: オクニ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kai (Conquest)
lore: Kai (Japanese: カイヒメ  Kaihime ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Aya (Conquest)
lore: Aya (Japanese: アヤゴゼン  Aya-Gozen ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kanetsugu
lore: Kanetsugu (Japanese: カネツグ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Magoichi
lore: Magoichi (Japanese: マゴイチ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Yukimura
lore: Yukimura (Japanese: ユキムラ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kunoichi
lore: Kunoichi (Japanese: クノイチ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Hanzō
lore: Hanzō (Japanese: ハンゾウ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Gracia
lore: Gracia (Japanese: ガラシャ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Muneshige
lore: Muneshige (Japanese: ムネシゲ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kanbei
lore: Kanbei (Japanese: カンベエ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . He, along with Hanbei , is one of Hideyoshi 's personal advisers and junior Warlords. Despite his appearance, Kanbei is the younger of the two.

title: Hanbei
lore: Hanbei (Japanese: ハンベエ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . He, along with Kanbei , is one of Hideyoshi 's personal advisors and junior Warlords. Despite his appearance, Hanbei is the older of the two.

title: Ieyasu
lore: Ieyasu (Japanese: イエヤス ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kotarō
lore: Kotarō (Japanese: コタロウ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Nō
lore: Nō (Japanese: ノウヒメ  Nōhime ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Ujiyasu
lore: Ujiyasu (Japanese: ウジヤス ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Yoshimoto
lore: Yoshimoto (Japanese: ヨシモト ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Kenshin
lore: Kenshin (Japanese: ケンシン ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Masamune
lore: Masamune (Japanese: マサムネ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Shingen
lore: Shingen (Japanese: シンゲン  Shingen ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Nene
lore: Nene (Japanese: ネネ  Nene ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Yoshihiro
lore: Yoshihiro (Japanese: ヨシヒロ  Yoshihiro ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Mitsuhide
lore: Mitsuhide (Japanese: ミツヒデ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Motonari
lore: Motonari (Japanese: モトナリ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Ginchiyo
lore: Ginchiyo (Japanese: ギンチヨ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Motochika
lore: Motochika (Japanese: モトチカ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Hideyoshi
lore: Hideyoshi (Japanese: ヒデヨシ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Oichi
lore: Oichi (Japanese: オイチ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest . She is partnered with the Hero / Heroine in the game's initial story, The Legend of Ransei .

title: Nobunaga
lore: Nobunaga (Japanese: ノブナガ ) is a Warlord in Pokémon Conquest .

title: Heroine
lore: The Heroine (Japanese: 主人公  Protagonist ) is a Warlord that appears in Pokémon Conquest if the player's selected gender is female. She is the only character in the game who can be named by the player, and is the main character under the player's control in the game's initial story, The Legend of Ransei . Her counterpart is the Hero .

title: Hero
lore: The Hero (Japanese: 主人公  Protagonist ) is a Warlord that appears in Pokémon Conquest if the player's selected gender is male. He is the only character in the game who can be named by the player, and is the main character under the player's control in the game's initial story, The Legend of Ransei . His counterpart is the Heroine .

title: Kōji Nishino
lore: Kōji Nishino (Japanese: 西野弘二  Nishino Kōji ) is a game designer of Pokémon games, currently working at Game Freak . He has been involved in nearly every main series Pokémon game since Pokémon Red and Green Versions . He has also assisted the animation producers for Lucario and the Mystery of Mew .

title: Shigeki Morimoto
lore: Shigeki Morimoto (Japanese: 森本茂樹  Morimoto Shigeki , born October 2nd, 1967 [ 1 ] [ 2 ] ) is a game designer, Pokémon designer, and programmer who has worked at Game Freak since 1992. [ 2 ] Morimoto has been involved in nearly every core series Pokémon game since Pokémon Red and Green . He was the game director for Pokémon Emerald and Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . Morimoto is notable for his prominent role in the creation of the Pokémon Mew , which has since become his favorite Pokémon. He also appears as an NPC called Morimoto (Japanese: モリモト ) in Generations  V , VII , and VIII .

title: Gym guide
lore: The Gym guide is a title in the core series  Pokémon games belonging to at least seven characters, each corresponding to a different region . In each case, the guide is usually found at the front of each Pokémon Gym , ready to offer tactical advice to novice Trainers . He congratulates the player upon defeating the Gym Leader , and offers more advice for the player's journey . He can occasionally be sarcastic. Some Gym guides do not stay inside their gyms. The Celadon Gym guide is never seen in his Gym, and instead appears at the Rocket Game Corner , where he plays the slot machines . Similarly, the Cianwood Gym guide is found in the city 's Pokémon Center instead of the Gym. The Petalburg Gym guide will vanish after the player has defeated Norman , and, in Generation II only, the Cinnabar Gym guide will arrive after Blaine has been defeated. In the Kanto -based games, there is a guide for the Indigo Plateau as well as for each Gym. Some games reveal the Gym guide's name:

title: Loblolly
lore: Loblolly (Japanese: シタン  Citan ) is a character in the Generation V  core series  games .

title: The Riches (Trainer class)
lore: The Riches (Japanese: ブルジョワールけ  Bourgeoir family ) are a family of seven living in Undella Town in Pokémon Black and White . Six members of the family, Draco, Susan, Clairdonna, Zillion, Trish, and Miles, can be battled; the seventh member is Draco's father, an item maniac who buys Relic items found in the Abyssal Ruins as well as flutes . In Pokémon Black and White, the player may challenge the family to battle once a day, and all battles for that day happen with no break between them. Originally, only Draco can be challenged, outside the villa. Once the player wins against Draco outside the villa and Draco moves inside the villa, whenever the player defeats every family member that was inside the villa when they started battling, a new family member will appear and challenge the player, until all six of the battling family members are around the table. A family member who has appeared will remain even if the player loses against them, meaning that the player may lose against a new family member one day, and encounter another new family member the next day. Once the player wins against Miles, the final battling family member, the player will not be able to challenge the family again. In Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 , the Riches' house has been demolished and a Maid states that they moved far away. The item maniac, however, is in a newly-built house on the original land plot. An NPC inside the house wonders why only the father stayed.

title: Emmet
lore: Subway Boss Emmet (Japanese: サブウェイマスタークダリ  Subway Master Kudari ) is one of the leaders of the Battle Subway in Pokémon Black, White , Black 2, and White 2 , along with his brother, Ingo .

title: Ingo
lore: Subway Boss Ingo (Japanese: サブウェイマスターノボリ  Subway Master Nobori ) is one of the leaders of the Battle Subway in Pokémon Black, White , Black 2, and White 2 , along with his brother, Emmet . In Pokémon Legends: Arceus , Ingo is the warden tasked with watching over a special Sneasler .

title: Charles
lore: Charles (Japanese: チャールズ  Charles ) is a motorcyclist from Driftveil City .

title: Bianca's father
lore: Bianca's father , or Bianca's dad , (Japanese: ベルパパ  Bel's papa ) is a non-player character that appears in Black and White .

title: Mom (Black and White)
lore: Mom (Japanese: おかあさん  mother ) is the mother of Hilbert or Hilda . She lives in Nuvema Town , and she met her husband while he was on his own Pokémon journey . Apparently she was once a Trainer and had a journey of her own. She mostly stays at home but leaves at one point to deliver the Running Shoes . Looker dresses up as her in the player's house after the defeat of Team Plasma . In Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 , much like Red 's mother in the Generation II games and Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver , she still resides in the same house and tells the player that her son or daughter is out in another region looking for N . If Memory Link has been activated, she will refer to her son or daughter by the player's name from the game the input Friend Code is from. Otherwise, she will not refer to them by a name, but rather as her child.

title: Hawes
lore: Hawes (Japanese: キダチ  Kidachi ) is Lenora 's husband and the assistant director of the Nacrene Museum .

title: Amanita
lore: Amanita (Japanese: ショウロ  Shōro ) is the storage system creator of the Unova region, who lives in Striaton City . She is an expert in computing, creating a Pokémon Storage System that succeeded Bebe 's storage system.

title: Anthea and Concordia
lore: Anthea (Japanese: 愛 の 女神  Goddess of Love , バーベナ  Verbena ) and Concordia (Japanese: 平和 の 女神  Goddess of Peace , ヘレナ  Helena ) are members of Team Plasma . They were adopted by Ghetsis when they were children and have taken care of N since then.

title: Shadow Triad
lore: The Shadow Triad (Japanese: ダークトリニティ  Dark Trinity ), each referred to individually as Shadow (Japanese: ダーク  Dark ), are three faithful servants of Ghetsis and N and are high-ranking members of Team Plasma . The Shadow Triad are completely loyal to Ghetsis because he once saved their lives.

title: Ryoku
lore: Ryoku (Japanese: リョクシ  Ryokushi ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Giallo
lore: Giallo (Japanese: ジャロ  Giallo ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Bronius
lore: Bronius (Japanese: スムラ  Sumra ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Gorm
lore: Gorm (Japanese: アスラ  Azula ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Zinzolin
lore: Zinzolin (Japanese: ヴィオ  Vio ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Rood
lore: Rood (Japanese: ロット  Rood ) is one of the Seven Sages of Team Plasma .

title: Ghetsis
lore: Ghetsis Harmonia Gropius (Japanese: ゲーチス・ハルモニア・グロピウス  G-Cis Harmonia Gropius [ 3 ] ) is the main villain in Pokémon Black, White , Black 2, and White 2 . He is one of the Seven Sages and the true mastermind behind Team Plasma .

title: N
lore: N (Japanese: Ｎ  N ) is a character in Pokémon Black, White , Black 2, and White 2 . In Pokémon Black and White, he is one of the player 's rivals [ 7 ] and the puppet leader of Team Plasma who aspires to create separate worlds for humans and Pokémon . His full name is Natural Harmonia Gropius (Japanese: ナチュラル・ハルモニア・グロピウス  Natural Harmonia Gropius ). [ 8 ]

title: Fennel
lore: Fennel (Japanese: マコモ  Makomo ) is a non-player character in the Generation V  core series  games . She is a friend of Professor Juniper who specializes in studying Pokémon Trainers and Pokémon dreams. She is sometimes referred to as Doctor Fennel ( マコモ博士  Dr. Makomo ).

title: Alder
lore: Alder (Japanese: アデク  Adeku ) is the Champion of the Unova region's Pokémon League in Pokémon Black and White .

title: Marshal
lore: Marshal (Japanese: レンブ  Renbu ) is a Fighting-type  Trainer and member of the Unova  Elite Four .

title: Grimsley
lore: Grimsley (Japanese: ギーマ  Gīma ) is a Dark-type  Trainer and member of the Unova  Elite Four .

title: Shauntal
lore: Shauntal (Japanese: シキミ  Shikimi ) is a Ghost-type  Trainer and member of the Unova  Elite Four .

title: Drayden
lore: Drayden (Japanese: シャガ  Shaga ) is the Gym Leader of Opelucid City 's Gym , known officially as the Opelucid Gym , and the mayor of Opelucid City. He specializes in Dragon-type  Pokémon and gives the Legend Badge to Trainers who manage to defeat him. In Pokémon White , Iris held the title of Opelucid City Gym Leader instead.

title: Iris
lore: Iris (Japanese: アイリス  Iris ) is a Dragon-type  Trainer . She was one of the Gym Leaders of Opelucid City 's Gym , known officially as the Opelucid Gym , giving out the Legend Badge , in Pokémon White . Two years later, in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 , she is the Champion of the Unova  region 's Pokémon League .

title: Brycen
lore: Brycen (Japanese: ハチク  Hachiku ) is an actor who is the Gym Leader of Icirrus City 's Gym , known officially as the Icirrus Gym . He specializes in Ice-type  Pokémon . He gives the Freeze Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Skyla
lore: Skyla (Japanese: フウロ  Huuro ) is a cargo pilot who is the Gym Leader of Mistralton City 's Gym , known officially as the Mistralton Gym . She specializes in Flying-type  Pokémon . She gives the Jet Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Clay
lore: Clay (Japanese: ヤーコン  Yakon ) is a businessman in the mining industry who is the Gym Leader of Driftveil City 's Gym , known officially as the Driftveil Gym . He specializes in Ground-type  Pokémon . He gives the Quake Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Elesa
lore: Elesa (Japanese: カミツレ  Kamitsure ) is a model who is the Gym Leader of Nimbasa City 's Gym , known officially as the Nimbasa Gym . She specializes in Electric-type  Pokémon . She gives the Bolt Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Burgh
lore: Burgh (Japanese: アーティ  Arty ) is an artist who is the Gym Leader of Castelia City 's Gym , known officially as the Castelia Gym . He specializes in Bug-type  Pokémon . He gives the Insect Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Lenora
lore: Lenora (Japanese: アロエ  Aloe ) is an archaeologist who is the Gym Leader of Nacrene City 's Gym , known officially as the Nacrene Gym . She specializes in Normal-type  Pokémon . She gives the Basic Badge to Trainers who defeat her. In addition to being the Nacrene City Gym Leader, Lenora is also the director of the Nacrene Museum .

title: Cress
lore: Cress (Japanese: コーン  Corn ) is one of the three Gym Leaders of Striaton City 's Gym , known officially as the Striaton Gym . He specializes in Water-type  Pokémon . He gives the Trio Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Chili
lore: Chili (Japanese: ポッド  Pod ) is one of the three Gym Leaders of Striaton City 's Gym , known officially as the Striaton Gym . He specializes in Fire-type  Pokémon . He gives the Trio Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Cilan
lore: Cilan (Japanese: デント  Dent ) is one of the three Gym Leaders of Striaton City 's Gym , known officially as the Striaton Gym . He specializes in Grass-type  Pokémon . He gives the Trio Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Cedric Juniper
lore: Cedric Juniper (Japanese: アララギパパ  Araragi-Papa ) is Professor Juniper 's father. He used to be a Pokémon researcher. According to Bianca , he specializes in Pokémon distribution and biology.

title: Professor Juniper
lore: Professor Aurea Juniper (Japanese: アララギ博士  Dr. Araragi ) is the resident Pokémon Professor of Nuvema Town in the Unova region. She specializes in the origins of Pokémon.

title: Bianca
lore: Bianca (Japanese: ベル  Bel ) is a Pokémon Trainer from the Unova  region . She is a rival character in Pokémon Black and White and an assistant to Professor Juniper in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 .

title: Cheren
lore: Cheren (Japanese: チェレン  Cheren ) is a rival character in Pokémon Black and White , and the Gym Leader of Aspertia City 's Gym , known officially as the Aspertia Gym , in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 . As a Gym Leader, he specializes in Normal-type  Pokémon . He gives the Basic Badge to Trainers who defeat him.

title: Hilda (game)
lore: Hilda (Japanese: トウコ  Touko ) is the female player character in Pokémon Black and White . Her male counterpart is Hilbert .

title: Hilbert (game)
lore: Hilbert (Japanese: トウヤ  Tōya ) is the male player character in Pokémon Black and White . His female counterpart is Hilda .

title: Supurna
lore: Supurna (Japanese: ツバサ  Tsubasa ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . She is a young woman who has a strong passion for Flying-type Pokémon, and even wears a Wingull themed outfit. She resides in the Aqua Resort on Sophian Island and has the ability to call down the Pokémon the player has captured in the sky with a pinwheel-like whistle. She also assigns the mission to calm down Articuno , Zapdos , and Moltres . After capturing Pokémon in the sky, by talking to her, the player can take them along as friend Pokémon.

title: Kasa
lore: Kasa (Japanese: ドレス  Dress ) is a member of the Societea in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . In the Sky Fortress, she battles the player with a Ditto that can transform into Raikou , Entei , and Suicune after she disguises herself as the player's partner and sets off various traps. She is first encountered in Aqua Resort . Her piece of the armor was stolen by Purple Eyes, and she was found by Murph while on board The Union.

title: Purple Eyes
lore: Purple Eyes (Japanese: パープルアイ  Purple Eye ) is the head admin of the Pokémon Pinchers . He appears in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs and is a rather experienced archaeologist. Also, according to Red Eyes , he is "the type to throw away something when he's done with it," as seen when he dumped Raikou 's Involith on Mt. Layuda .

title: Hocus (Ranger)
lore: Hocus (Japanese: マジック  Magic ) is a talented magician and a member of the Societea in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He uses a giant Crobat when faced in the Sky Fortress, after using his skills to trap the Ukulele Pichu in a box and create a confusing battleground. He is first encountered in Tilt Village , performing magic tricks for a group of children. His piece of the armor was stolen by Purple Eyes, and he was found by Murph while on board The Union.

title: Kira
lore: Kira (Japanese: キーア  Kea ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . She lives in the past of Cocona Village . Kira is Tanvir 's partner and a former Steelhead oracle, but she gave up when she started to argue with Tanvir. She has a brother called Thane, one of the Steelheads of the Fire Temple , who attacks the player with a Blaziken . She will allow the player to enter temples in the past and acts somewhat like Ravio 's caretaker.

title: Red Eyes
lore: Red Eyes (Japanese: レッドアイ  Red Eye ) is one of the Pokémon Pinchers admins. He appears in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs .

title: Blue Eyes
lore: Blue Eyes (Japanese: ブルーアイ  Blue Eye ) is one of the three Pokémon Pinchers admins. She appears in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs .

title: Burkhart
lore: Burkhart (Japanese: ビゲロー  Bigelow ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . Burkhart is first introduced at the Wireless Tower on Renbow Island , where he is shocked by electricity. He offers to charge the player's Capture Styler but Rand intervenes, due to it being unsafe as well as voiding the warranty. However, the player can still speak to him afterwards to recharge the Styler. Later, he tips off the player to the Pinchers' takeover of the abandoned warehouse on Hinder Cape . He is in charge of the repairs to the tower after Raikou destroyed it during the Pokémon Pinchers ' takeover.

title: Leanne
lore: Leanne (Japanese: レイラ  Leila ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . She is an archaeologist who is studying the connection between the ruins and fairy tales of the Oblivia region. The player first meets her at the Wireless Tower with her husband, Rand . After the player has obtained the symbol for Raikou , Leanne investigates the symbol and figures out its meaning. She is later kidnapped by Purple Eyes and held hostage by Steelheads in the Oblivia Ruins . She eventually discovers the secret of the Rainbow Grail and the Rainbow Dais and finds out how to stop the Sky Fortress from destroying the entire region of Oblivia with a tsunami.

title: Rand
lore: Rand (Japanese: タルガ  Talga ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He is the Area Ranger in charge of patrolling the Oblivia region at the beginning of the game. Rand lives on Renbow Island with his wife Leanne and daughter Nema . He is first met by the player at the Wireless Tower on top of Mt. Latolato , where he asks the player to help him save the Radio Base from the Pokémon Pinchers who have taken it over. He then accompanies the player on many important missions and appears in many places, such as the Oblivia Ruins to get his wife and daughter back and the Sky Fortress . Rand, with the help of one of his daughters inventions, manages to tamper with the Super Plasma Cannon on the Sky Fortress saving Renbow Island from destruction. He is temporarily sucked into a void by Purple Eyes 's Mewtwo while sacrificing his life for Edward 's sake while on the Sky Fortress. He is later brought back by Mewtwo and goes with Leanne to a conference in another region.

title: Nema
lore: Nema (Japanese: パネマ  Panema ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs .

title: Nixie
lore: Nixie (Japanese: ミナモ  Minamo ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . She is found at Lapras Beach . She is friends with Lapras and will allow the player to travel out to Coral Sea . When the player meets Nixie for the first time, she is having an argument with Nema , who is trying to get Nixie to let her ride on Lapras into Coral Sea to obtain a UFO that crashed there. Eventually, the player is allowed access to the Coral Sea.

title: Ravio
lore: Ravio (Japanese: ヘリオ  Helio ) is a character in the past of Oblivia 's Cocona Village . Ravio's father is the Steelhead of the Light Temple , known as Ellios, and one of his friends is Celebi . He meets the player when the player is taken into the past by Celebi. He, along with Tanvir and Kira , explain how the past works and about the temples and their oracles. Later, he sneaks into Teakwood Forest without Kira's permission and is kidnapped by Sabios of the Dark Temple , who states that Ellios is under his control.

title: Edward
lore: Edward (Japanese: エドワード  Edward ), also known as Ed "The Thinker" , is the Societea 's leader in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He faces the player in the Sky Fortress as a boss with Mewtwo , who he controls by using armor that originally belonged to Sabios of the Dark Temple .

title: Arley
lore: Arley (Japanese: アックス  Axe ) is a member of the Societea in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He's a large man who boasts incredible strength. In the Sky Fortress, he battles the player with a Regigigas after putting the player through a swarm of angry Pokémon. He is first met in Rasp Cavern . His piece of the armor was stolen by Purple Eyes, and he was found by Murph while on board The Union . In the past, he was a wrestler known as "Arley the Destroyer".

title: Nick (Ranger)
lore: Nick (Japanese: ニック  Nick ) is a resident of Cocona Village that appeared in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He is introduced after Booker brings the player to his house on Renbow Island . Nick works as an apprentice in wood craftsmanship under Booker's care, a mentor who is strict but sees great potential in his pupil. Nick also has a habit of repeated pessimism, often thinking too critically of himself or the conditions of others, which Booker jokingly refers to as "daynightmares".  When Pichu 's ukulele is broken by Pokémon Pinchers , Booker sends Nick to retrieve wood from Dolce Island , asking the player to escort him. While getting the wood, Nick accidentally steps on a group of sleeping Sunkern . Later on Nick will upgrade the ukulele Pichu's instrument making its assist last longer and more effective. He later helps Booker repair the Ranger Union's ship, The Union, after the player returns from Blue Eyes ' submarine. He built the bridge in the Latolato Trail , which was christened "The Over the Creek in the Green Forest, the Red-and-White-Striped, Wonderfully Crafted, Raikou Safe with No Creaking, Renowned All Over the World for Connecting Yesterday and Tomorrow and Proudly-Built-by-Nick Bridge" by Ralph and Nema .

title: Ralph (Ranger)
lore: Ralph (Japanese: ラーフ  Raph ) is a green-haired boy that appears in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . He is Booker 's grandson. He accompanies the player at various points in the game, such as in the first trip to Rasp Cavern and around Cocona Village . He also appears in various quests.

title: Booker
lore: Booker Hastings (Japanese: ブッカー シンバラ  Booker Shinbara ) is a resident of Cocona Village from Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . Booker, an expert carpenter, is first met shortly after the player washes up on Dolce Island where he was investigating UFOs that were flying around the island. After he introduces himself, Booker offers to take the player to his home in Cocona Village in an unfinished boat of his. Booker has a grandson, Ralph , who also lives in Cocona Village. Later on in the story he is called upon to fix Big Booker Bridge after the Pokémon Pinchers damage it. He makes ships for a living along with his apprentice Nick . In case the waves get high on Dolce Island , he looks after the Pokémon unable to swim or fly by creating refuge boats on the island to keep them safe. When the Pokémon Pinchers damage the Big Booker Bridge , he notably repairs it in a short amount of time, which is attributed to him designed the bridge. One of his prized ships is The Union , which later on in the game is docked at the Tilt Village harbor for the player to use. Another creation of Booker is Ukulele  Pichu 's ukulele, which was made of spare ship material. He gave Pichu the ukulele as a token of his gratitude for making him feel better whenever he got tired of creating the boats on Dolce Island . Pichu's nickname of Ukulele Pichu was also given to it by Booker. Booker also assisted in evacuating the Pokémon from Dolce Island just before the Sky Fortress vaporized it.

title: Ukulele Pichu
lore: Ukulele Pichu (Japanese: ウクレレピチュー  Ukulele Pichu ) is a ukulele -playing Pichu that serves as the partner Pokémon to Ben or Summer in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . Its physical appearance is no different from an ordinary Pichu, other than the fact that it carries a ukulele on its back. The ukulele that it carries was made by Booker out of wood from the leftover parts of a boat, as mentioned early in the game, but after one of the Pokémon Pinchers breaks it, Booker makes a new, stronger one for it out of a special type of wood.

title: Summer (Ranger)
lore: Summer (Japanese: ミナミ  Minami ) is the female player character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . Her male counterpart is Ben .

title: Ben (Ranger)
lore: Ben (Japanese: ナツヤ  Natsuya ) is the male player character in Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs . His female counterpart is Summer .

title: Spiky-eared Pichu
lore: Spiky-eared Pichu (Japanese: ギザみみピチュー  Gizamimi Pichu ) is a Pichu . Its form is different from the one of an ordinary Pichu, as it has three spikes at the tip of its left ear, hence its name.

title: Cameron (Johto)
lore: Cameron the Photographer (Japanese: ゲンゾー  Genzō ) is a non-player character in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . After the player arrives in Goldenrod City , Cameron can be found in both Kanto and Johto on varying days of the week , and in a few cases, at different times. He will take pictures of the player's party and the surrounding area. Cameron's house is in Cianwood City , which has an automatic camera beside it for use at all times; however, Cameron cannot be found here.

title: Mr. Game
lore: Mr. Game is a non-player character in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . He can first be seen in the Goldenrod Game Corner , and later at the Celadon Game Corner . The first time the player speaks to him, he will give them a Coin Case . Because of a difference between language releases in Generation IV, he appears only in non-Japanese games. Mr. Game owns the two Game Corners in the Kanto and Johto regions, having taken over the Celadon Game Corner at some point after Team Rocket 's defeat in Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen . The games played in this renovated Game Corner (and its counterpart in Goldenrod) are unique to HeartGold and SoulSilver. Voltorb Flip , which was invented by Mr. Game, replaces the slot machines from previous games. Mr. Game loves watching people play his Coin game, and comments that it is what he lives for. He challenges the player to participate, saying "Make my heart pound with excitement!".

title: Jet
lore: Jet (Japanese: ジェット  Jet ) is a character from Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver .

title: Maximo
lore: Maximo (Japanese: ケジメ  Kejime ) is the host of the Pokéathlon . He can be seen at the Pokéathlon Dome in HeartGold and SoulSilver and is there to explain the Pokéathlon and its events as well as himself. He is nicknamed "big brother", despite having an older twin brother, Primo .

title: Magnus
lore: Magnus (Japanese: コブシ  Kobushi ) is the founder of the Pokéathlon Dome in Johto , located near to the National Park .

title: Lyra (game)
lore: Lyra (Japanese: コトネ  Kotone ) is the female player character in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . Her male counterpart is Ethan . She replaces Kris from Pokémon Crystal .

title: Ketch Appy
lore: Ketch Appy (Japanese: ケッチちゃん  Ketch-chan ), often referred to as Pokétch Detective Ketch Appy (Japanese: ポケッチデカのケッチちゃん  Pokétch Detective Ketch-chan ), is a minor character introduced in Pokémon Platinum . She is the star of her own television program aired on Jubilife TV , in which she is often billed as a "child prodigy". In the program, she is a detective who uses the Pokétch to solve crimes. However, most of her plans are usually disrupted by errors she makes in using it, such as forgetting that the Memo Pad app resets if the app on the Pokétch is changed. In this way, her program often serves to give tips on how to use the various apps.

title: Battle Hall
lore: The Battle Hall (Japanese: バトルステージ  Battle Stage ) is a facility located in the northwestern corner of the Battle Frontier in Generation IV . The stadium is a huge catwalk , in where people walk down the catwalk to the battleground, while fans take a number of photos and the spotlights shine all over the place. There is also a red carpet on the floor, all the way from the entrance to the stadium.

title: Argenta
lore: Argenta (Japanese: ケイト  Kate ) is the Frontier Brain in charge of running the Battle Frontier 's Battle Hall . She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Hall Matron (Japanese: ステージマドンナ  Stage Madonna ).

title: Caitlin
lore: Caitlin (Japanese: カトレア  Cattleya ) is a Psychic-type  Trainer and member of the Unova  Elite Four . She is also the head of the Battle Castle in the Battle Frontier that appeared in Pokémon Platinum and HeartGold and SoulSilver , where she is known as Lady Caitlin (Japanese: カトレアおじょうさま  Miss Cattleya ).

title: Darach
lore: Darach (Japanese: コクラン  Kokuran ) is the Frontier Brain in charge of serving the Battle Frontier 's Battle Castle . Darach is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Castle Valet (Japanese: キャッスルバトラー  Castle Butler ).

title: Dahlia
lore: Dahlia (Japanese: ダリア  Dahlia ) is the Frontier Brain in charge of running the Battle Frontier 's Battle Arcade . She is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Arcade Star (Japanese: ルーレットゴーデス  Roulette Goddess ).

title: Thorton
lore: Thorton (Japanese: ネジキ  Neziki ) is the Frontier Brain in charge of running the Battle Frontier 's Battle Factory , acting under the title of Factory Head (Japanese: ファクトリーヘッド  Factory Head ).

title: Charon
lore: Charon (Japanese: プルート  Pluto ) is one of Team Galactic 's four Commanders , introduced in Pokémon Platinum . He appears to be related to Choy , due to their resemblance. However, the exact relationship between the two is unknown.

title: Looker
lore: " Looker " (Japanese: ハンサム  Handsome ) is the codename of an International Police officer who travels the world investigating various villainous teams. He was introduced in Pokémon Platinum as an International Police officer investigating Team Galactic . He has since appeared multiple times throughout the core series , namely in Pokémon Black and White , Pokémon X and Y , Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire , Pokémon Sun and Moon , and Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon , frequently investigating the activities of villainous teams .

title: Club Look-See
lore: Club Look-See (Japanese: みてみて☆クラブ  Look-Look Club ) is a club of ranch owners in My Pokémon Ranch . Occasionally, a member of Club Look-See will visit a player's Ranch and show the player their Ranch. Each member's ranch has its own theme. It should be noted that each of the member's Miis are designed to look somewhat like the Pokémon they take care of. Without the Platinum update, Club Look-See has 37 members. After obtaining the Japan-exclusive update, the number of members has increased to 40; additionally, players can also return to the various ranches at any time they want. Once the cycle has been completed once (i.e. each member's ranch is visited once in order), the members return again at periodic intervals, albeit not in order.

title: Hayley
lore: Hayley (Japanese: ユカリ  Yukari ) is a friend of Bebe and the host of My Pokémon Ranch . Her appearance seems to be based on a midwestern American farmer. Her appearance in-game is created from the Wii 's Mii avatar system. Every day that the player visits their ranch, Hayley brings a Pokémon to the ranch. Sometimes she will bring a special Pokémon that she will trade to the player in exchange for a Wanted Pokémon . These Pokémon may know moves as the result of breeding or by using a Technical Machine . She also gives the player a Phione in exchange for a Leafeon when the Ranch reaches level 15, and a Mew in exchange for an Egg when it reaches level 25.

title: Herbert
lore: Herbert (Japanese: クサノ  Kusano ) is a non-player character from Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia who is a researcher for the Ranger Union . Professor Hastings has asked him to research Grass-type  Pokémon . He will ask the player through a Ranger Quest to bring him certain Pokémon so he can research them. Herbert will first appear in Altru Park , requesting that the player bring him an Oddish so he can research it. He will then appear in Shiver Camp , requesting that the player bring back an Abomasnow . Finally, he will appear in Haruba Village requesting a Cacturne . He will not be found after this quest.

title: Brighton Hall
lore: Brighton Hall (Japanese: アプライト・ホール  Upright Hole ) is a character from the game Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . He was the second president of Altru Inc. , the son of Doyle Hall and the father of Blake Hall . While the oil fields were beginning to run low he started drilling at Chroma Highlands , and by chance found the Shadow Crystal , which was being guarded by Darkrai . He became allured by the darkness, and changed his son's name from Wyatt to Blake in front of the crystal. He later realized that that was a mistake, but Blake took over Altru and drove him out before he could do anything about it. His last known wish was for the Tears of Princes to be brought close to the Shadow Crystal, which would release his son from the darkness. His name was an inspiration for Operation Brighton, due to the information obtained from his diary. His diary is found by the player at Altru Ruins . The diary is damaged and becomes completely illegible a few pages in. It is taken back to the Ranger Union , where Professor Hastings and the other scientists try to restore it, giving the player valuable information over the course of the game. Upon the defeat of Blake Hall, Professor Hastings returns the diary to Blake.

title: Mr. Kaplan
lore: Mr. Kaplan (Japanese: キャプス  Caps ) is a character in Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia and a teacher at the Ranger School . He often jokes about being part of "Team School" and how they will someday rule the world. The player first meets him after the entrance exam. He teaches the fundamentals of capture by having the player capture a Pikachu . He keeps a book on his desk called Drama for Beginners , which may imply he enjoys acting. Mr. Kaplan may also be the husband of Ms. Claire , as two children living in Pueltown tell the player that their parents teach Target Clearing and capturing at the Ranger School. His name may come from his teaching of "Capture."

title: Oscar (Ranger)
lore: Oscar (Japanese: パトリ  Patri ) is a non-player character from Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia who collects "exquisite fragrances". He will ask the player through a Ranger Quest to bring him certain Pokémon so he can collect their scents. Oscar will first appear in Boyleland , requesting that the player bring him a Muk so he can collect its aroma. He will then appear in Haruba Village , requesting that the player bring back a Weezing and a Skuntank for their fragrances as well. After this quest, he informs the player that he will leave for other regions in search of new fragrances. He will not be found after this quest.

title: Vatona and Nage
lore: Vatona and Nage are minor characters in the game Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . Vatona is Nage's older brother and their father, Mr. Stubborn, lives on the Union Road . They worked together with Professor Hastings to create the Fine Styler and the Micro Aqualung, as well as the world's only Vatonage Styler . Even though their father hates science, he somehow found it fitting that he named his sons Vatona and Nage , from the word vatonage , as they created the Vatonage Styler.

title: Big Bertha
lore: Big Bertha (Japanese: ビッグママ  Big Mama ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . She is frequently hailed as the strongest person in Almia , even beating Barlow , according to Crawford . She is the wife of Little Tim as well as the mother of four children, and owner of a Miltank . She is also famous for her Milk Pudding. Her hometown is located in Vientown . She is seen now and again throughout the game, involved in minor parts of the plot as well as a few Ranger Quests . Her first appearance is while the player is going to Nabiki Beach. When the player is a student it is possible to visit her house. It is located in the southwest of Vientown with the Miltank in the pasture. She is seen during the first Mission, where the player must deliver the Vien Tribune to the citizens of Vientown and Chicole Village . Later, she plays a much bigger role at Nabiki Beach when the Vientown Rangers need enough strength to carry a Gigaremo unit . She is later seen giving milk pudding to the Rangers, even showing kindness to Ollie . That made him speak to the Rangers after all the days that he didn't say a word. Then Big Bertha insisted that the rope was cut. Later on in the game, she congratulates the player for becoming the Top Ranger on the player's way home. In a quest, she asks the player to bring a Slakoth to her husband so that his fear of Pokémon would go away.

title: Little Tim
lore: Little Tim (Japanese: リトルパパ  Little Papa ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . He is a milkman and runs a dairy farm with his family in Vientown . He is first met at the Ranger School where he is attacked by two wild Bidoof and is saved by the player and Keith . He is the husband of Big Bertha , the father of four children, and the owner of a Miltank . It is revealed during one of the Ranger Quests that he has been afraid of Pokémon ever since he was scratched by a Slakoth as a small child. This fear has developed into a belief that all Pokémon want to attack him. During said Quest, his wife asks the player to bring a Slakoth to him so that his fear would go away. Later, he tells the player that he's now able to pat Bidoof on their heads.

title: Henry
lore: Henry (Japanese: シニア  Senior ) is a non-player character in Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia .

title: Kyle (Ranger)
lore: Kyle (Japanese: カイト  Kaito ) is a character in the game Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia .

title: Brook
lore: Brook (Japanese: ハシモト  Hashimoto ) is a minor character in the game Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . Brook operates the Norward Bridge linking Pueltown and Altru Park . He is often quick to rush into things and doesn't think things through. He is involved in minor parts of the plot, as well as a Ranger Quest .

title: Mimi (Ranger)
lore: Mimi is a character from Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia .

title: Mr. Woodward
lore: Mr. Woodward (Japanese: キボリじいさん  Old Man Kibori ) is a character from the game Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia . He is first seen Nabiki Beach , with a Starly , a Munchlax , and a Pachirisu , one of which later joins the player as the partner Pokémon . He resides in Vientown next to the farm of Big Bertha , and is a well known woodcutter. His house is full of logs and artistic painting on wood, including a wooden statue of a Pikachu , which "looks as if it could come to life." After the forest fire, he would also ask the player to clear away some fallen logs in Vien Forest . After completing a quest, Ponte shows Mr. Woodward a sculpture of a Probopass , and while Mr. Woodward stated that the sculpture wasn't very good, he realized that Ponte had a lot of spirit. Mr. Woodward then accepts Ponte as his apprentice.

title: Ms. Claire
