He lives in what appears to be a Junk Shop, run by his grandfather, Makan . The bottom floor is a maze of old machine parts, gadgets and other items. The second floor contains a desk and a few more seemingly random objects. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , he and Makan move the Junk Shop to Gateon Port . Among their accomplishments in XD are fixing Gateon's moving bridges, upgrading Michael 's scooter into a hoverscooter suitable for traveling in the desert, and building the Robo Kyogre . He is also featured on a wanted poster in the Pyrite Town Police Station; the reason for this is unknown.

title: Megg
lore: Megg (Japanese: シホ  Shiho ) is a member of the Kids Grid and lives with her older brother, Nett , in The Under . She has a Shroomish but it is unknown if she or any of the kids in Pyrite Town and The Under have any other Pokémon. After Nett sends Wes a photo, to test the P★DA 's capabilities beyond e-mail, Megg believes it was a photo of herself sent, leaving her embarrassed. She's glad to learn it wasn't a photo of her, saying she doesn't look very good in them. After hearing about Wes and Rui , Megg is joyful when she finally meets them. She looks up to Wes and Rui as inspirational heroes.  She worries about them when they go to places such as the headquarters of Cipher . In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , she is the secretary and official guide for ONBS . She gets captured by Cipher members during the invasion of the ONBS, but is later rescued by the player .

title: Bitt
lore: Bitt (Japanese: クロ  Kuro ) is a character in Pokémon Colosseum and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . He is a member of the Kids Grid in Colosseum. He is first encountered standing guard at the door of the Kids Grid, waiting for the Powerup Part . In XD: Gale of Darkness, he has become part of the ONBS with most other Kids Grid members.

title: Nett
lore: Nett (Japanese: スレッド  Thread ) from The Under is the genius of Kids Grid . His home and place of operation has a large, rotating antenna dish on top. Nett is Megg 's older brother. His name is based on "network," as he runs the Kids Grid computer network. His Japanese name may be read as "Thread," the name of a string of messages on one topic in an online message forum. Wes first meets Nett when asked by Perr to deliver a powerup part to him. The part is necessary to get the Kids Grid back up and running again. Nett's job becomes to decipher a data ROM containing a list of Shadow Pokémon that have been made, and to keep Wes updated on his findings via P★DA . Nett also relays sightings of Shadow Pokémon from people visiting from Pyrite Town . When Wes travels to the Deep Colosseum , it's up to Nett to keep him informed about the Deep King and his Pokémon, including the Deep King's Shadow Shuckle . He informs Wes when the Deep king enters the knockout tournament, and implores the Trainer to enter and show up the king. In Pokémon XD , Nett and the Kids Grid own and run a successful TV station, ONBS . Michael meets him when he needs to bring a Data Rom to him. Nett is usually found on top of the ONBS building.

title: Secc
lore: Secc (Japanese: レン  Ren ) is a boy who lives in Pyrite Town . He appears in both Pokémon Colosseum and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . He operates from a back room in Duking 's house and he is simply a friend of Duking's daughter. Secc establishes contact with Nett in The Under via his computer. He helps in founding the Kids Grid . He gets Wes 's P★DA number and, later, contacts Wes after the defeat of Evice . Secc, along with Nett, both become valuable sources of information regarding Cipher 's plot and are instrumental in bringing the syndicate down. They act as Wes's main sources of information, apparently because children are often overlooked when they overhear things. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, he, along with other Kids Grid members, has founded a TV station, ONBS .

title: Marcia
lore: Marcia (Japanese: レイラ  Leila ) is a character in Pokémon Colosseum and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . In Pokémon Colosseum, Marcia is first seen in the back of her father Duking 's house in Pyrite Town . She is part of the Kids Grid , and plans to recover Duking's stolen Plusle . Her role is greatly expanded in Pokémon XD. Marcia has now become a reporter for ONBS and has a reputation for being reckless. She and her cameraman, Cameran, are encountered leaving Pyrite on Michael's first visit en route to a news story at Phenac City . However, when she fails to come back, Michael is sent to find her. Marcia and Cameran are eventually found being held hostage by Snattle in Phenac Stadium , where the Cipher Admin is trying to intimidate her into handing over their videotapes of the evil activities within Phenac. As Michael fights Snattle, Marcia and Cameran tape the battle and later run it on ONBS, exposing Cipher to all of Orre. Later, she can be found outside the Cipher Key Lair , where she and Cameran are reporting on Chief Sherles 's plans to arrest the Cipher members inside.

title: Silva
lore: Silva (Japanese: シルバ  Silva ) is a young man from Pyrite Town who is widely considered as Duking 's best friend, lieutenant, and right-hand man. Brave, loyal, but more than a little foolhardy and luckless. Silva attempts to fight Cipher throughout Pokémon Colosseum but has little luck. When Miror B. kidnapped Duking's Plusle and used it to intimidate Duking into letting Cipher have free run of the town, Silva made a rescue attempt. Silva snuck into the Pyrite Bldg , but was eventually thwarted and injured by two of Miror B.'s lackeys, Reath and Ferma . Following that, Silva was rescued by Wes and Rui , who arrived in the nick of time. Silva continued to investigate Cipher's actions in Orre , though. He later attempted to explore the Under , but was captured when he was mistaken for Wes. While captured, he gives Wes an R-Disk . He was eventually freed after Wes liberated the Under from the control of Venus . Silva later disguised himself as a Cipher security guard and infiltrated Realgam Tower . In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , Duking has handed Silva the responsibility of running Pyrite Colosseum . However, he plays no other significant role in this game. He is shown to have an apparent interest in cosplay , specifically as a Plusle; Silva becomes embarrassed when the player discovers a Battle CD that features Plusle in his bookshelf, attempting to deny that he owns it to learn how to make a Plusle costume before giving it to the player. He also talks about dressing up in disguises at other times, continuing on from when he disguised himself to infiltrate Realgam Tower in the previous game.

title: Fateen
lore: Fateen (Japanese: ビーディ  Beedy ) is an old woman who runs a fortunetelling business at the very entrance of Pyrite Town in Orre . She does this by scrying in a crystal ball in order to give advice to others and tell their fortunes. She is known as the "Mother of Pyrite Town". She gets almost as much respect from the town's citizens as Duking .  Everyone in town knows her and has asked for her advice at one time or another.  Many Pokémon Trainers ask her if they will win battles or tournaments; others ask about romance. Although Fateen appears at first the stereotypical trickster, she does possess actual psychic talent. She is the one who gives Wes and Rui the first clue about how to purify Shadow Pokémon and directs them to Agate Village . Furthermore, she later points them in the direction of The Under . She may also be approached many times throughout the game in order to receive clues as to what to do next that are from what she sees in the crystal ball. Fateen appears again in Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , this time playing no role other than giving Michael clues as to where to go next. Once 82 Shadow Pokémon have been snagged , Fateen will exclaim that there is "something beyond even [her] sight", which she can only describe as "[a]n immense round thing " "[a]top a lighthouse ".

title: Officer Johnson
lore: Officer Johnson (Japanese: ユイト  Yuito ) is a bumbling and hyperactive though determined police officer who patrols Pyrite Town , under the command of Chief Sherles . Despite his efforts, he is not very bright or effective, and he often ends his sentences with the word "Pow". Throughout the Shadow Pokémon incident in Orre , Officer Johnson would dash into the Police Station, usually smacking into Wes and Rui while they discussed some urgent matter with Chief Sherles. Johnson would then proceed to tell Wes, Rui, and the Chief something they already knew. During the events of the game, Chief Sherles eventually puts Johnson to guard the Cipher members that Duking arrested. However, they manage to escape when Johnson is not paying attention. In Pokémon XD , Johnson is still obsessing over his duty and his plan to get Chief Sherles's position which doesn't go well. Johnson was supposed to keep an eye on a Chaser and a Team Snagem Member locked up in the jail cells, but fails his task, resulting in the Team Snagem member escaping the cell. Sherles, being done letting Johnson mess things up, locked him up in a cell as his punishment. Johnson has not left the cell since. No matter how much he begs Sherles to let him out, Sherles ignores him.

title: Chief Sherles
lore: Chief Sherles (Japanese: ヘッジ署長  Chief Hedge )  is the much-overworked police chief of Pyrite Town . He has the help of Officer Johnson in his job of keeping the crime of the town under control. In Pokémon Colosseum , Sherles is first seen sitting in his police office, where he warns Wes and Rui of the uncontrollable lawlessness in Pyrite and asks that they leave town for their safety. He also appears to investigate the windmill after Silva steals one of the generator's gears and comments on Silva's motives for doing so. Finally, Sherles appears to arrest Evice and Nascour at Realgam Tower during the ending. Sherles appears in Pokémon XD , but he plays no significant role aside from being a familiar face. After defeating Snattle , however, he reveals news that Cipher's previous boss, Evice , was only a regional boss, hinting at Greevil 's position as Cipher's Grand Master. After defeating Greevil, Sherles can be found outside the Cipher Key Lair , where he is in the act of arresting the remaining Cipher members.

title: Cail
lore: Cail (Japanese: マサ  Masa ) is an NPC who appears in Pokémon Colosseum and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . He has green hair and wears a black jumpsuit. He stands at the entrance of Pyrite Town for the duration of the game and will battle Wes several times throughout it. He is a good but unwilling source of information who only "spills the beans" upon being defeated in battle. He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Rogue (Japanese: ゴロツキ  Rogue ).

title: Justy
lore: Justy (Japanese: セイギ  Seigi ) is a young man who is renowned for being one of the best professional Pokémon Trainers in Orre . Justy has built up a large fan following, especially in Phenac City . For most of the young Pokémon Trainers in Phenac City, defeating Justy is the ultimate goal. He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  PreGymLeader (Japanese: トレトレリーダー  TraiTrai Leader ), which is formatted as Pre-Gym Leader in Pokémon Colosseum: Prima's Official Strategy Guide . [ 1 ]  Justy is the Gym Leader of the Prestige Precept Center , often referred to as the Pre Gym, in Phenac City; however, the Prestige Precept Center isn't an official Gym as it's not sponsored by a Pokémon League and doesn't hand out a Badge to winners. However, because Orre doesn't have a Pokémon League of its own due to the overall lack of many wild Pokémon or population, the Prestige Precept Center can be considered the closest thing Orre has to a proper Pokémon Gym . In Pokémon Colosseum , Justy can be found in the Pre Gym upon Wes's first visit to Phenac City. After speaking to him, Justy will allow Wes to fight four of his students in succession. Upon completion, Justy rewards Wes with a White Herb and tells him to come back with six Pokémon. Upon returning with six Pokémon, Justy will fight Wes himself. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , when Michael arrives in Phenac City after visiting Realgam Tower, six identical Justys will come walking out of the Pre Gym and spread out all over the city. Finding each "Justy" will reveal them as one of the Hexagon Brothers in disguise, and each one will drop a Battle CD upon defeat in battle. The real Justy can be found locked up in the Pre Gym's basement with all of the other captured citizens. After he is rescued and Cipher has been forced out of Phenac City, Justy can be challenged in battle. According to one of his students, he seems to slightly favor his Nosepass over his other Pokémon. He relies on evasion -raising moves and Abilities such as Double Team and Sand Veil . Justy gives out TM27 ( Return ) to Trainers who defeat him in Pokémon Colosseum , and in Pokémon XD , Trainers who defeat him will receive TM32 ( Double Team ) and a Lum Berry . He will only fight Trainers who have a complete team of six Pokémon.

title: Willie
lore: Willie (Japanese: ウイリー  Willie ) is a Rider who appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He first meets Wes at the Outskirt Stand where he is sitting at a table in the restaurant area. He predicts that Wes is a strong Trainer who would beat him in a battle. Eventually, when Wes leaves the stand, Willie challenges him to a battle, which Wes wins. Willie will challenge Wes again after Wes has reached Pyrite Town . A third battle can be fought with him after Wes has Snagged all 48 Shadow Pokémon . Willie stands outside the train at Outskirt Stand for the duration of the game. He is the first Trainer that the player may face. Unlike most male Riders, Willie has a unique appearance, having being pink hair and slightly differently-colored clothes. Willie also battles the player at the Outskirt Stand in Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . He is the only Trainer in the game outside of Colosseum challenges to have battle music from the original game.

title: Mayor Es Cade
lore: Es Cade (Japanese: バックレー  Backley ) is the mayor of Phenac City in Pokémon Colosseum . A fat and jolly gentleman, he is worried about the crimes being committed by Cipher and Team Snagem .

title: Nascour
lore: Nascour (Japanese: ジャキラ  Jakira ) is a man with a terrifying visage. He is gaunt, dressed in dark clothes and possesses wiry, gray, serpentine hair. He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Cipher (Japanese: シャドー  Shadow ). Nascour's strategy in battle is to use X Special and other stat-enhancing items on his Pokémon.

title: Fein
lore: Fein (Japanese: フェイク  Fake ) is a Cipher Peon who appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He is encountered after Wes has snagged 47 of the 48 Shadow Pokémon in the game. A series of emails on Wes's P★DA regarding his attacking people (most notably, Athlete Dash in Phenac City ) with a Shadow Togetic , leads Wes to Outskirt Stand where he encounters an impostor of himself, dressed to look identical to him down to the very last feature. He is known as Shady Guy during battle, and his name will be the same as the player character 's own. Upon being defeated, he reveals himself to be Fein, a Cipher Peon and a master of disguise. He wanted to tarnish Wes's reputation around Orre ; while he partially succeeds in making Wes unpopular with some of Phenac City's citizens for a short while, after watching the next TV broadcast, the citizens forgive Wes, realizing it was an impostor who did it and not Wes himself. Fein is the final opponent that can be battled in Pokémon Colosseum's post-game. Fein can be rebattled until his Shadow Togetic is snagged and he is beaten, after which he will vanish for good. When viewing the Snag List entry for Togetic, his Trainer class is listed as Fake Hero .

title: Mirakle B.
lore: Mirakle B. (Japanese: ミラクルボ  Miraklebo ) is a minor villainous character in Pokémon Colosseum . He is the self-proclaimed successor to Miror B. . He is only beginning to work on an afro. He has colored his helmet to look like a Poké Ball , in imitation of Miror B.'s afro. Like Miror B., his suit is yellow and his boots are white. He has bronze sunglasses and a red scarf. His theme music is a sped-up, off-key version of Miror B.'s theme. He appears at the Pyrite Cave in the place of Miror B. after Miror B. himself has been defeated. He can only be battled before defeating Evice ; afterwards, Reath and Ferma will be in the cave instead.

title: Bluno
lore: Bluno (Japanese: ブルーノ  Bluno ) is a Cipher Peon who appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He is first encountered at the Mayor's House in Phenac City along with Verde , Rosso , Miror B. , Folly , and Trudly . Leaving Wes to Folly and Trudly, Miror B. departs for Pyrite Town . Upon beating Folly and Trudly, Wes exits the Mayor's House to find the three Peons blocking the exits to the city. Bluno occupies the spot in front the city's main, southern entrance. Wes must choose one of the three Peons to battle. The other two run away and disappear for quite some time. If he chooses to fight Bluno, he will be known as a Mystery Troop member rather than as a Cipher Peon. If Wes snags Bluno's Shadow Croconaw, but loses all his Pokémon before the end of the battle , he may attempt to fight an alternate Peon, but they will not carry their Shadow Pokémon. If Wes chooses to fight Bluno in Phenac City, he will appear for a rematch in Realgam Tower disguised as a receptionist behind the desk in the tower's casino. After he is beaten by Wes he vanishes and is not seen again. Should Wes choose to fight Verde or Rosso in Phenac City then Bluno will not show up until after beating the game in one of the Snagem Hideout or Shadow PKMN Lab (chosen at random). He is dressed uniquely as compared to most other male Cipher Peons. His outfit is a much darker blue than what the usual peon wears.

title: Rosso
lore: Rosso (Japanese: ロッソ  Rosso ) is a Cipher Peon who appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He is first encountered at the Mayor's House in Phenac City along with Bluno , Verde , Miror B. , Folly and Trudly . Leaving Wes to Folly and Trudly, Miror B. departs for Pyrite Town . Upon beating Folly and Trudly, Wes exits the Mayor's House to find the three Peons blocking the exits to the city. Rosso occupies the spot in front the city's eastern entrance. Wes must choose one of the three Peons to battle. The other two run away and disappear for quite some time. If Wes chooses to fight Rosso, he will be known as a Mystery Troop member during the first battle rather than a Cipher Peon. If Wes snags Rosso's Shadow Quilava, but loses all his Pokémon before the end of the battle , he may attempt to fight an alternate Peon, but they will not carry their Shadow Pokémon. If Wes chooses to fight Rosso in Phenac City, he will appear for a rematch in Realgam Tower disguised as a receptionist behind the desk in the tower's casino. After he is beaten by Wes he vanishes and is not seen again. Should Wes choose to fight Verde or Bluno in Phenac City, Rosso will not show up until after beating the game in either Snagem Hideout or the Shadow PKMN Lab (chosen at random) He is dressed uniquely as compared to most other Cipher Peons. His outfit is red, rather than the usual light blue.

title: Verde
lore: Verde (Japanese: ベルデ  Verde ) is a Cipher Peon who appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He is first encountered at the Mayor's House in Phenac City along with Bluno , Rosso , Miror B. , Folly and Trudly . Leaving Wes to Folly and Trudly, Miror B. departs for Pyrite Town . Upon beating Folly and Trudly, Wes exits the Mayor's House to find the three Peons blocking the exits to the city. Verde occupies the spot in front the city's western entrance. Wes must choose one of the three Peons to battle. The other two run away and disappear for quite some time.  If he chooses to fight Verde, he will be known as a Mystery Troop member during the first battle rather than a Cipher Peon. If Wes snags Verde's Shadow Bayleef, but loses all his Pokémon before the end of the battle , he may attempt to fight an alternate Peon, but they will not carry their Shadow Pokémon. If Wes chooses to fight Verde in Phenac City, he will appear for a rematch in Realgam Tower disguised as a receptionist behind the desk in the tower's casino. After he is beaten by Wes he vanishes and is not seen again, unless Shadow Bayleef wasn't snagged. Should Wes choose to fight Bluno or Rosso in Phenac then Verde will show up in either Snagem Hideout or Shadow PKMN Lab (chosen at random) after beating the game. He is dressed uniquely as compared to most other Cipher Peons. His outfit is green, rather than the usual light blue.

title: Skrub
lore: Skrub (Japanese: コワップ  Kowap ) is a Cipher Peon that appears in Pokémon Colosseum . He is dressed uniquely as compared to most other male Cipher Peons. His uniform is gray rather than the normal light blue and he wears a blue neckerchief. His helmet is also a different shape to the others. He is initially assigned to the command of Cipher Admin  Dakim , who sends him to Agate Village to destroy the Relic Stone under the advisement of fellow Cipher Admin Ein , as the Relic Stone had the potential to disrupt Cipher's Shadow Pokémon scheme. Skrub was put in command of three other Cipher Peons for the mission. There, he encounters Wes and is defeated by him, having his Shadow Hitmontop  snagged in the process. He flees and is encountered again at Mt. Battle after Wes has defeated Dakim. The Cipher Admin orders Skrub to report to the Shadow PKMN Lab to directly assist Ein. Once Wes has defeated the six other Cipher Peons in the lab, he encounters Skrub guarding the door to Ein's room. Skrub battles Wes and loses. He flees once more. After Evice has been defeated, Skrub appears for the last time at Snagem Hideout , being the second Cipher Peon to drop from the ceiling to challenge Wes. He loses again and is not seen further.

title: Ferma
lore: Ferma (Japanese: スーラ  Seurat ) is a Miror B.Peon . In Pokémon Colosseum , she is never seen without her partner Reath . They are first seen in a cinema sequence with Miror B., who exits and leaves the Pyrite Bldg in their guard. Wes arrives at the building and defeats Reath, snagging her shadow  Remoraid in the process; he then defeats Ferma and snags her Mantine , saving Silva , who Reath and Ferma had been holding captive. Ferma and Reath show up again in Pyrite Town 's jail, Folly and Trudly having moved to separate cells nearby. Wes gets the Jail Key and steals the Elevator Key from Reath, who is lying on the cell's bed, asleep. Once Wes has beaten Evice , all four prisoners escape. Ferma and Reath both flee to the room in Pyrite Cave where Miror B. is fought. They battle with Wes and then remain there. Their actual status as members of Cipher is foggy; they may not know the entire plan, but only what Miror B. tells them.

title: Reath
lore: Reath (Japanese: ブレス  Breath ) is a Miror B.Peon . In Pokémon Colosseum , she is never seen without her partner Ferma . They are first seen in a cinema sequence with Miror B., who exits and leaves Pyrite Bldg in their guard. Wes arrives at the building and defeats Reath, snagging her shadow  Remoraid in the process; he then defeats Ferma and snags her Mantine , saving Silva , who Reath and Ferma had been holding captive. Reath and Ferma show up again in Pyrite Town 's jail, Folly and Trudly having moved to separate cells nearby. Wes gets the Jail Key and steals the Elevator Key from Reath, who is lying on the cell's bed, asleep. Once Wes has beaten Evice , all four prisoners escape. Reath and Ferma both flee to the room in Pyrite Cave where Miror B. is fought. They battle with Wes and then remain there. Their actual status as members of Cipher is foggy; they may not know the entire plan, but only what Miror B. tells them.

title: Trudly
lore: Trudly (Japanese: トロイ  Troy ) is a Miror B.Peon .

title: Folly
lore: Folly (Japanese: ヘボイ  Heboy ) is a Miror B.Peon .

title: Ein
lore: Ein (Japanese: ボルグ  Borg ) is one of the original four Cipher Admins . A cruel and callous young scientist, he is long on ambition and short on emotion. He is obsessed with the idea of creating an insanely powerful Pokémon at any cost which he managed to do with amazing results. In battle, Ein prefers to use Rain Dance , then Thunder . He protects his Water-type and Flying-type Pokémon from Electric-type moves by often having a Pokémon with Lightningrod out on the field. He also likes using Toxic and Protect to dodge attacks while the poison damage increases each turn.

title: Venus
lore: Venus (Japanese: ヴィーナス  Venus ) is one of the original four Cipher Admins . Considering herself a pop idol and diva, she's dressed in layers of pink silk and carries a crescent moon on her back. She's obsessed with being popular and attractive to The Under civilians. Some people dislike her for this, but the rest of the Under civilians consider her very beautiful. In battle, Venus's favorite strategy is to use Attract and layer other status effects to impair a Pokémon's ability to attack or defend itself.

title: Dakim
lore: Dakim (Japanese: ダキム  Dakim ) is one of the four Cipher Admins in Pokémon Colosseum . He is a hulking, muscle-bound man with red hair, and wears a necklace full of Poké Balls . Dakim is shown to be very reckless. He usually tries to keep his cool, but can become dangerous when angered. Dakim is the only Cipher Admin not directly involved in the creation and distribution of Shadow Pokémon . Instead, he and his underlings appear to be used as general enforcers and muscle. He himself has incredible physical strength, and he'll physically attack any enemy who won't give in to his demands. He also has surprisingly good jumping abilities, as he flees with a powerful and very big leap. In battles, Dakim prefers to have one of his two Pokémon use Protect , while the other uses Earthquake . He alternates his Pokémon's actions every turn. This is less prevalent in later battles, as he starts to utilize Pokémon that have the Levitate Ability, although members of his team without said Ability will still use Protect. He also may use an X Accuracy to increase the accuracy of his attacks. Later, some of his Pokémon use the Sunny Day / Solar Beam combination.

title: Miror B.
lore: Miror B. (Japanese: ミラーボ  Mirābo ) is a recurring character and major antagonist from Pokémon Colosseum and Pokémon XD . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Wanderer (Japanese: さすらい  Wanderer ).

title: Wakin
lore: Wakin (Japanese: ヤッチーノ  Yaccino ) is a member of Team Snagem . He is second in command to Gonzap . In Pokémon Colosseum , he and two unnamed Team Snagem grunts, likely Agrev and Biden , encounter Wes in Phenac City . They demand that Wes return the Snag Machine that he stole from Snagem Hideout . Wakin battles Wes with his Koffing and Corphish and loses. He and the two Snagem grunts leave and he is not seen again in the game. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness , along with Biden and Agrev steal Michael 's Snag Machine to help resurrect Team Snagem. When Michael confronts Gonzap, he has Wakin battle the player. After Wakin is beaten, Michael must defeat Gonzap in order to recover the Snag Machine. He does so and gets the Snag Machine back along with Gonzap's Key. In XD, Wakin's model is swapped with Agrev 's.

title: Biden
lore: Biden (Japanese: ザブ  Zabu ) is a member of Team Snagem . In Pokémon Colosseum he and Agrev helped Gonzap lure Wes back to Snagem Hideout after he had caught the three Shadow  first partner Pokémon . He helped spread rumors that the large Snag Machine had been fixed. Wes fell for the trap and returned to Snagem Hideout. Biden battled Wes with his team of four Smeargle , one of which was a Shadow Pokémon that Wes managed to Snag . After Wes defeated him he stated if he had won, he would have knocked Wes out and had his Smeargle paint on his face. Biden is one of the two Team Snagem members who has a unique appearance. His eyes are drawn differently from generic ones. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness Biden, along with Agrev and Wakin , stole Michael 's Snag Machine and brought it back to Snagem Hideout to help resurrect Team Snagem. Michael defeated Gonzap to recover the Snag Machine.

title: Agrev
lore: Agrev (Japanese: ミサンゴ  Misango ) is a member of Team Snagem . In Pokémon Colosseum he, along with Biden helped Gonzap lure Wes back to Snagem Hideout after he had caught the three Shadow  first partner Pokémon . He helped spread rumors that the large Snag Machine had been fixed. Wes fell for the trap and returned to Snagem Hideout. Agrev battled Wes, his team included a Shadow Ursaring which Wes managed to Snag . Agrev is notable as being one of only two Team Snagem grunts to have a unique look: his consists of black sunglasses over his eyes. In Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness Agrev, along with Biden and Wakin stole Michael 's Snag Machine and brought it back to Snagem Hideout to help resurrect Team Snagem. Michael defeated Gonzap to recover the Snag Machine. For reasons unknown, Agrev and Wakin's models were swapped.

title: Gonzap
lore: Gonzap (Japanese: ヘルゴンザ  Helgonza ) is the leader of Team Snagem , a band of criminals operating in Orre . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Snagem Head (Japanese: スナッチ団ボス  Team Snatch Boss ).

title: Rui
lore: Rui (Japanese: ミレイ  Mirei ) is a mysterious young girl with psychic abilities.  She is Wes 's friend and the sidekick and deuteragonist in Pokémon Colosseum .  She's determined, caring, and brave, but can be a bit bossy and stubborn at times. In the game manual, she is referred to as Partner . [ 1 ]

title: Wes
lore: Wes (Japanese: レオ  Leo ) is a young man who lives in the Orre region of the world . He is the protagonist of Pokémon Colosseum . In the game manual, he is referred to as Hero . [ 2 ]

title: Brigette
lore: Brigette (Japanese: アズサ  Azusa ) is the older sister of Lanette and the host of Pokémon Box Ruby & Sapphire and Pokémon Bank , as well as the developer of the latter. [ 2 ]

title: Trick Master
lore: The Trick Master (Japanese: カラクリ 大王  King of Tricks ) is a character in Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire . He lives on Route 110 in the Trick House .

title: Old guys
lore: The old guys (Japanese: オヤジたち  old guys ) are a quintet of non-player characters that appear in Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire . They differ in the color of their hair and clothing. They all appear in the Mauville City  Pokémon Center , though only one will be present at a time. In Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, they also appear in Mauville Hills later.

title: Peeko
lore: Peeko (Japanese: ピーコちゃん  Peeko-chan ) is a female Wingull owned by Mr. Briney . She appears in Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , as well as in the manga and in animation .

title: Move Reminder
lore: A Move Reminder (Japanese: 技思い出し  Move Reminder ) or Pokémon Move Maniac (Japanese: ポケモンわざマニア  Pokémon Move Maniac ), also known as a Move Tutor in English and sometimes called a move relearner by fans, is a character who can teach a Pokémon any move that its species is able to learn by leveling up, and from Generation VI onward, special moves that it has forgotten (such as Egg Moves ). The Move Reminder usually requires a Heart Scale in exchange for their services. They first appeared in Generation III . In Pokémon Sword and Shield , Jack provides Move Reminder services free of charge (among other services). From Pokémon Legends: Arceus onward, the Move Reminder is no longer an NPC in the game, and instead a Pokémon's moves can be changed at any time outside of battle by going into the Moves section in a Pokémon's summary.

title: Mom (Hoenn)
lore: Mom (Japanese: おかあさん  mother ) is the mother of Brendan or May and the wife of Norman .

title: Kiri
lore: Kiri (Japanese: キリ  Kiri ) is a young girl living in Sootopolis City who gives out two Berries each day the player talks to her. In Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald , she gives one Berry from among the Pomeg , Kelpsy , Qualot , Hondew , Grepa , Tamato , Cornn , Magost , Rabuta , or Nomel Berries, the other from the Figy or Iapapa specimens. In Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire , her first Berry is one from among the Pomeg , Kelpsy , Qualot , Hondew , Grepa , Tamato , Cornn , Magost , Rabuta , or Nomel Berries, while her second is one from the Figy , Wiki , Mago , Aguav , Iapapa , and Razz Berries.

title: Fossil Maniac
lore: The Fossil Maniac (Japanese: 化石 マニア  Fossil Maniac ) is a character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald and Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . His house is located on Route 114 , just outside Fallarbor Town . The Fossil Maniac's brother, who also lives in his house, will hand out TM28 ( Dig ). In Pokémon Emerald, after the National Pokédex is obtained, the player can go to the Desert Underpass through his house, where the unchosen Fossil can be obtained. The sign outside his house in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald states: In Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, the sign states: When checking on the display case inside, it states the following:  Rocks in peculiar shapes fill the display cases.

title: Treasure Hunter
lore: The Treasure Hunter (Japanese: トレジャーハンター  Treasure Hunter ), known as the Diving Treasure Hunter in Generation III , is a non-player character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire who exchanges shards for Evolution stones . He lives in a small hut on Route 124 , near Mossdeep City .

title: Shelly
lore: Shelly (Japanese: イズミ  Izumi ) is one of the Admins of Team Aqua .

title: Matt
lore: Matt (Japanese: ウシオ  Ushio ) is one of the Admins of Team Aqua .

title: Archie
lore: Archie (Japanese: アオギリ  Aogiri ) is the head of Team Aqua . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer classes  Aqua Leader (Japanese: アクアだんリーダー  Team Aqua Leader ) and Team Aqua (Japanese: アクアだん  Team Aqua ).

title: Courtney
lore: Courtney (Japanese: カガリ  Kagari ) is one of the Admins of Team Magma .

title: Tabitha
lore: Tabitha (Japanese: ホムラ  Homura ) is one of the Admins of Team Magma .

title: Maxie
lore: Maxie (Japanese: マツブサ  Matsubusa ) is the head of Team Magma . He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer classes  Magma Leader (Japanese: マグマだんリーダー  Team Magma Leader ) and Team Magma (Japanese: マグマだん  Team Magma ).

title: Dock
lore: Dock (Japanese: ツガ  Tsuga ) is a character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald and Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire who plays a minor role in the story. He works at Stern's Shipyard and was commissioned to design a ferry.

title: Captain Stern
lore: Captain Stern (Japanese: クスノキ館長  Director Kusunoki ) is an oceanographer who lives in Slateport City .

title: Winstrate family
lore: The Winstrate family (Japanese: カチヌキファミリー  Kachinuki family ) are a family of five who are obsessed with Pokémon battles and battling. The family consists of father Victor, mother Victoria, daughter Vivi, son Vito, and grandmother Vicky. The Winstrates live in a house on Route 111 , north of Mauville City . Vito is not at home, however, as he has left to challenge the Pokémon League .

title: Wanda
lore: Wanda (Japanese: ミチル  Michiru ) is Wally 's cousin that lives in Verdanturf Town .

title: Rydel
lore: Rydel (Japanese: カゼノ  Kazeno ) is a character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire who owns the Mauville City  Bicycle Shop .

title: Professor Cozmo
lore: Professor Takao Cozmo (Japanese: ソライシ・タカオ博士  Dr. Takao Soraishi ) is a character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire . He is a meteoriticist who lives in Fallarbor Town .

title: Gabby and Ty
lore: Gabby (Japanese: マリ  Mari ) and Ty (Japanese: ダイ  Dai ) are a pair of co-workers who can be found interviewing  Trainers all over Hoenn . Gabby is an interviewer and Ty is her trusty cameraman.

title: Lanette
lore: Lanette (Japanese: マユミ  Mayumi ) is a computer technician and the younger sister of Brigette . She lives in a house on Route 114 near Fallarbor Town and is the maintainer of Hoenn's Pokémon Storage System . She first appears in Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire and reappears in Pokémon Emerald and Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire .

title: Wally
lore: Wally (Japanese: ミツル  Mitsuru ) is one of the two rival characters in Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire , Emerald , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , the other being Brendan / May . In Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, Wally in his later battles possesses a Gallade that can Mega Evolve with his handmade wooden Mega Pendant, which holds his Key Stone . The Mega Pendant is shaped like a Gallade's head. Wally is a young, sickly boy who lives in Petalburg City . Despite his illness, his dream is to train Pokémon . In his room, in Petalburg City, there are a lot of books about how to raise and battle with Pokémon covered in sticky notes, a notebook which has been written and erased again and again and a terrestrial globe with pins in places in the Kalos and Unova regions, suggesting that he has been wanting to go outside and catch Pokémon for a long time.

title: Mr. Stone
lore: Joseph Stone (Japanese: ツワブキ・ムクゲ  Mukuge Tsuwabuki ), usually referred to as Mr. Stone (Japanese: ツワブキ社長  President Tsuwabuki ), is the president of the Devon Corporation and father of Steven Stone .

title: Mr. Briney
lore: Mr. Briney (Japanese: ハギ 老人  Old Man Hagi ) is a skilled sailor who appears in many forms of the media.  He has a Wingull named Peeko .

title: Steven Stone
lore: Steven Stone (Japanese: ツワブキ・ダイゴ  Daigo Tsuwabuki ) is a skilled Trainer who specializes in Steel-type  Pokémon . He is the Champion of the Hoenn  region 's Pokémon League in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire , as well as the Hoenn League Champion during Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . A collector of rare stones, Steven is the son of the president of the Devon Corporation , and makes his home in Mossdeep City . In the Hoenn-based games, he wanders the region, aiding the player on their journey . In Pokémon Emerald , he is a former Champion, with Wallace taking his place.

title: Drake
lore: Drake (Japanese: ゲンジ  Genji ) is a Dragon-type  Trainer and member of the Hoenn  Elite Four .

title: Glacia
lore: Glacia (Japanese: プリム  Purim ) is an Ice-type  Trainer and member of the Hoenn  Elite Four .

title: Phoebe
lore: Phoebe (Japanese: フヨウ  Fuyou ) is a Ghost-type  Trainer and member of the Hoenn  Elite Four .

title: Sidney
lore: Sidney (Japanese: カゲツ  Kagetsu ) is a Dark-type  Trainer and member of the Hoenn  Elite Four .

title: Wallace
lore: Wallace (Japanese: ミクリ  Mikuri ) is a highly accomplished Trainer and Coordinator who specializes in Water-type  Pokémon . In the original Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire , as well as their remakes , Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire , he is the Gym Leader of Sootopolis City 's Gym , known officially as the Sootopolis Gym , awarding the Rain Badge to those who defeat him. In Emerald , he becomes Champion of the Pokémon League and gives the Gym back to Juan , his former instructor. Wallace also excels in Pokémon Contests and, in Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, can be encountered in Master Rank  Beauty Contests . He is apparently close to Steven Stone , and assists him in the Cave of Origin quest in Ruby, Sapphire, Omega Ruby, and Alpha Sapphire. He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Sootopolitan (Japanese: ルネのたみ  Citizen of Rune ) and the only character in the animated series to be referred to as a Contest Master (Japanese: コンテストマスター  Contest Master ).

title: Tate and Liza
lore: Tate (Japanese: フウ  Fū ) and Liza (Japanese: ラン  Lan ) are the twin Gym Leaders of Mossdeep City 's Gym , known officially as the Mossdeep Gym . They specialize in Psychic-type  Pokémon . They give the Mind Badge to Trainers who defeat them. They are the only characters in the games to have the Trainer class  Leaders (Japanese: ジムリーダー  Gym Leader ).

title: Winona
lore: Winona (Japanese: ナギ  Nagi ) is the Gym Leader of Fortree City 's Gym , known officially as the Fortree Gym . She gives out the Feather Badge to Trainers who defeat her. She specializes in Flying-type  Pokémon .

title: Norman
lore: Norman (Japanese: センリ  Senri ) is the father of the player and the Gym Leader of Petalburg City 's Gym , known officially as the Petalburg Gym in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald and their Generation VI remakes Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . He is an expert of Normal-type  Pokémon , and hands out the Balance Badge to any Trainer who defeats him.

title: Flannery
lore: Flannery (Japanese: アスナ  Asuna ) is the Gym Leader of Lavaridge Town 's hot springs Gym , known officially as the Lavaridge Gym . She specializes in Fire-type  Pokémon and gives out the Heat Badge to Trainers who defeat her.

title: Wattson
lore: Wattson (Japanese: テッセン  Tessen ) is the Gym Leader of Mauville City 's Gym , known officially as the Mauville Gym . Trainers who defeat him receive the Dynamo Badge . He is a jolly old man who specializes in Electric-type  Pokémon .

title: Brawly
lore: Brawly (Japanese: トウキ  Touki ) is the Gym Leader of Dewford Town 's Gym , known officially as the Dewford Gym . Trainers who defeat him receive the Knuckle Badge . He is a young surfer who specializes in Fighting-type  Pokémon .

title: Roxanne
lore: Roxanne (Japanese: ツツジ  Tsutsuji ) is the Gym Leader of Rustboro City 's Gym , known officially as the Rustboro Gym . Trainers who defeat her receive the Stone Badge . She is a scholar who specializes in Rock-type  Pokémon .

title: Professor Birch
lore: Professor Birch (Japanese: オダマキ博士  Dr. Odamaki ) is the resident Pokémon Professor of Littleroot Town and the Hoenn  region . He specializes in Pokémon  habitats and distribution.

title: May (game)
lore: May (Japanese: ハルカ  Haruka ) is the female choice for the player character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald and their Generation VI remakes, Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . She also serves as a rival in the same games if the player chooses to play as her male counterpart, Brendan .

title: Brendan (game)
lore: Brendan (Japanese: ユウキ  Yuuki ) is the male choice for the player character in Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire , and Emerald and their Generation VI remakes, Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire . He also serves as a rival in the same games if the player chooses to play as his female counterpart, May .

title: GR5 (TCG GB)
lore: GR5 (Japanese: GR5号  GR Number 5 ) is an Enigmatic Mask of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Unlike other members of Team GR, GR5 never battles the player at any point during the game, instead merely serving as a road-block, preventing access to GR Island . He appears at the Pokémon Dome , taunting the player as the Grand Masters are held hostage on GR Island. Meanwhile, at the Airport , GR5 stops the player from advancing if they have not obtained all four GR Coin pieces. Later, when the player has the whole GR Coin, he operates the blimp that goes between the two Trading Card Game Islands . He will then remain at the Airport, no longer appearing at the Pokémon Dome.

title: Queen (TCG GB)
lore: Queen (Japanese: クィーン ) is the fifth and final Dungeon Master in the Card Dungeon, located within the Game Center in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! When battled, Queen will ask the player to wager either 50 or 100 Coins on the outcome of the battle; refusing will cause the player to immediately leave the dungeon. Players who defeat Queen receive double the amount wagered. Win or lose, the player will leave the dungeon after the game is completed.

title: Rook (TCG GB)
lore: Rook (Japanese: ルーク ) is the fourth of five Dungeon Masters in the Card Dungeon, located within the Game Center in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! When battled, Rook will ask the player to wager either 30 or 50 Coins on the outcome of the battle; refusing will cause the player to immediately leave the dungeon. Players who defeat Rook receive double the amount wagered and go on to face Queen ; losing to Rook forces the player to leave the dungeon.

title: Bishop (TCG GB)
lore: Bishop (Japanese: ビショップ ) is the third of five Dungeon Masters in the Card Dungeon, located within the Game Center in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! When battled, Bishop will ask the player to wager either 10 or 30 Coins on the outcome of the battle; refusing will cause the player to immediately leave the dungeon. Players who defeat Bishop receive double the amount wagered and go on to face Rook ; losing to Bishop forces the player to leave the dungeon.

title: Knight (TCG GB)
lore: Knight (Japanese: ナイト ) is the second of five Dungeon Masters in the Card Dungeon, located within the Game Center in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! When battled, Knight will ask the player to wager either 10 or 20 Coins on the outcome of the battle; refusing will cause the player to immediately leave the dungeon. Players who defeat Knight receive double the amount wagered and go on to face Bishop ; losing to Knight forces the player to leave the dungeon.

title: Pawn (TCG GB)
lore: Pawn (Japanese: ポーン ) is the first of five Dungeon Masters in the Card Dungeon, located within the Game Center in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! When battled, Pawn will ask the player to wager 10 Coins on the outcome of the battle; refusing will cause the player to immediately leave the dungeon. Players who defeat Pawn receive 20 Coins (double the wager) and go on to face Knight ; losing to Pawn forces the player to leave the dungeon.

title: Yui (TCG GB)
lore: Yui (Japanese: ユイ ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Yui can be found in the ninth and final statue in the main room. Players who defeat Yui will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Anna (TCG GB)
lore: Anna (Japanese: アンナ ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Anna can be found in the eighth of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Anna will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Masquerade (TCG GB)
lore: Masquerade (Japanese: マスカレード ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Masquerade can be found in the seventh of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Masquerade will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Dee (TCG GB)
lore: Dee (Japanese: ディー ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Dee can be found in the sixth of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Dee will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Pierrot (TCG GB)
lore: Pierrot (Japanese: ピエロ ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Pierrot can be found in the fourth of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Pierrot will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Toshiron (TCG GB)
lore: Toshiron (Japanese: トシロン ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Toshiron can be found in the third of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Toshiron will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Magician (TCG GB)
lore: Magician (Japanese: マジシャン ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Magician can be found in the second of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Magician will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Eiji (TCG GB)
lore: Eiji (Japanese: エイジ ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Eiji can be found in the first of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Eiji will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Tobi-chan (TCG GB)
lore: Tobi-chan (Japanese: とびちゃん ) is one of the Ghost Masters located in the Sealed Fort , located on GR Island in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! Tobi-chan can be found in the fifth of the nine statues in the main room. Players who defeat Tobi-chan will obtain a Present Pack, which can consist of any card that can be found in a booster pack in the game.

title: Tap (TCG GB)
lore: Tap (Japanese: タップ  Tap ) is one of the Trainers at the GR Lightning Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . However, he is not a member of Team Great Rocket . When defeated, he gives out one of both Legendary Power and Beginning Pokémon booster pack.

title: Rui (TCG GB)
lore: Rui (Japanese: ルイ  Rui ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Her duelist class is Team GR Big Boss ( GR団 大かんぶ ), the same as Kanzaki . She appears for the first time in Mr. Ishihara's Villa . Mark or Mint must defeat her in a card duel at the GR Castle , as well as Kanzaki, to gain access to their king, Biruritchi . However, Rui has a special set of rules, and she will use different decks for any condition she chooses at random. When defeated, Rui gives the player one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Sky Flying Pokémon booster packs.

title: Kanzaki (TCG GB)
lore: Kanzaki (Japanese: カンザキ  Kanzaki ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . His duelist class is Team GR Big Boss ( GR団 大かんぶ ), the same as Rui . Mark or Mint must defeat him in a card duel at the GR Castle , as well as Rui, to gain access to their king, Biruritchi . However, he will refuse to battle the player if their deck does not contain all of the Legendary Cards , as Kanzaki wished to pit his own strength against these cards. When defeated, Kanzaki gives the player one of both We Are Team Rocket and Psychic Battle booster packs.

title: Biruritchi (TCG GB)
lore: Biruritchi (Japanese: ビルリッチ  Biruritchi ) is the creator of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . His duelist class is Team GR King (Japanese: GR団キング ).

title: Samejima (TCG GB)
lore: Samejima (Japanese: サメジマ  Samejima ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the Colorless Altar . He refuses to duel against the player unless this has four cards of the type he has chosen at that time (he can request either Jigglypuff , Dratini , or Mysterious Fossil cards). When defeated, he gives out two Psychic Battle booster packs.

title: Nishijima (TCG GB)
lore: Nishijima (Japanese: ニシジマ  Nishijima ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the Colorless Altar . He refuses to duel against the player unless this has four cards of the type he has chosen at that time (he can request either Pidgey , Spearow , or Double Colorless Energy cards). When defeated, he gives out two Legendary Power booster packs.

title: Ishii (TCG GB)
lore: Ishii (Japanese: イシイ  Ishii ), also known as the Enigmatic Mask  GR2 (Japanese: GR2号  GR Number 2 ), is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of Colorless Altar from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Like a couple other Team Great Rocket members, he has disguised himself behind a mask with a pattern across it so little can be said about his real appearance. After the player has first met Nikki at Mr. Ishihara's House , he appears at either the Grass Club (if the player is female) or Science Club (if the player is male), where he may be challenged in a 6-prize duel. His deck focuses on and Pokémon. After defeating him, the player is awarded with one of both We Are Team Rocket and Legendary Power booster packs and one piece of the Great Rocket Coin. The player meets him again at the Colorless Altar, where he is the Fort Leader. His deck, Eye of the Storm Deck , focuses on Pokémon, mainly on the ones that are of the Flying-type in the main games. He refuses to duel against the player unless they have four cards of the type he has chosen at that time (he can request either Rattata , Meowth , or any Dark Pokémon cards). When defeated there, he gives out two Island of Fossil booster packs and, if the player has defeated both Nishijima and Samejima , the GR Colorless Coin, also known as Snorlax Coin, which grants the player to enter Team GR Castle if they also have the GR Psychic Coin.

title: Ryōko (TCG GB)
lore: Ryōko (Japanese: リョウコ  Ryōko ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She's one of the Trainers at the GR Psychic Stronghold and is the Fort Leader  Mami 's daughter. She will not duel against the player if this has any Trainer Cards in the active deck. When defeated, she gives out one of both We Are Team Rocket and Island of Fossil booster packs.

title: Yōsuke (TCG GB)
lore: Yōsuke (Japanese: ヨウスケ  Yōsuke ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He is one of the Trainers in the GR Psychic Stronghold . Yōsuke refuses to duel against the player unless their deck has at least six Gastly and Haunter cards in total— Dark Haunter cards do not count toward this total. When defeated, he gives out one of both We Are Team Rocket and Legendary Power booster packs.

title: Miwa (TCG GB)
lore: Miwa (Japanese: ミワ  Miwa ), also known as the Enigmatic Mask  GR4 (Japanese: GR4号  GR Number 4 ), is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Like a couple other Team Great Rocket members, she has disguised herself behind a mask with a symbol on it, so little about her real appearance can be said. In Pokémon Card GB 2, she has taken control of the Psychic Club . Right after defeating the original Psychic Club Master, Murray , she can be challenged in a 6-prize duel. When she is defeated, the player is given one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Island of Fossil booster packs and one piece of the Team Great Rocket coin. She appears again in the GR Psychic Stronghold . She can be challenged to a duel, but only if the player's deck has only Energy cards. She uses the Direct Hit Deck . When defeated, she hands out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Beginning Pokémon booster packs.

title: Kevin (TCG GB)
lore: Kevin (Japanese: ケビン  Kevin ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He is one of the Trainers at the GR Psychic Stronghold . In all battles against him, the Low Resistance (Japanese: 抵抗力ていか  Lower Resistance ) rule is active. thus every Pokémon's Resistance to is -10 instead of -30. When defeated, he gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Legendary Power booster pack.

title: Mami (TCG GB)
lore: Mami (Japanese: マミ  Mami ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of the GR Psychic Stronghold from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is Ryōko 's mother. In all battles against her, the Energy Return (Japanese: エネルギーリターン  Energy Return ) rule is active, thus discarded Energy cards are returned to the player's hand. When defeated, she gives out two Team Rocket's Ambition booster packs and the GR Psychic Coin, also known as Mew Coin, which grants the player to enter Team GR Castle if the player also has the GR Colorless Coin. Also, she frees Grand Master  Rod .

title: Gōda (TCG GB)
lore: Gōda (Japanese: ゴウダ  Gōda ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the GR Fighting Fort . He will not duel against the player if this has any Energy Removal or Super Energy Removal cards in the active deck. When defeated, he gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Psychic Battle booster packs. He and Grace must be beaten before the player can challenge Kamiya , the Fort Leader . When the player defeats him for the first time, he frees the imprisoned Club Master  Mitch .

title: Grace (TCG GB)
lore: Grace (Japanese: グレース  Grace ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She's one of the Trainers at the GR Fighting Fort . She will not duel against the player unless this uses a deck with only  Energy cards . When defeated, she gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and Sky Flying Pokémon booster packs. She and Gōda must be beaten before the player can challenge Kamiya , the Fort Leader . When the player beats her for the first time, she reveals a chest containing a rare Dugtrio card.

title: Kamiya (TCG GB)
lore: Kamiya (Japanese: カミヤ  Kamiya ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of GR Fighting Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . In all duels against him, the Earth Power (Japanese: だいちのちから  Earth Power ) rule is active, thus every Pokémon's Resistance to is omitted. When defeated, he gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and We Are Team Rocket booster packs and the GR Fighting Coin, also known as the Machamp Coin, which grants the player the access to the northeast parts of the GR Island . The first time Mark or Mint meet Kamiya, he will demand that they first challenge his two pupils, Grace and Gōda , hidden in the maze of the Fighting Fort. Until this task is completed, he will refuse to challenge Mark or Mint.

title: Aira (TCG GB)
lore: Aira (Japanese: アイラ  Aira ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the GR Water Fort . In all duels against him, the Small Bench (Japanese: せまいベンチ Narrow Bench ) rule is active, thus no more than three Benched Pokémon are allowed at any time. When defeated, he gives out one Team Rocket's Ambition booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, he lets the player advance to the next room, allowing the player to reach Kanoko , the Fort Leader of GR Water Fort.

title: Senta (TCG GB)
lore: Senta (Japanese: センタ  Senta ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the GR Water Fort . He will not duel against the player unless they use a deck with 4 Magikarp cards. When defeated, he gives out one Psychic Battle booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, he frees the imprisoned Grand Master  Jack and puts a bridge over the water to make it possible to go to the next room, allowing the player to reach Aira .

title: Miyajima (TCG GB)
lore: Miyajima (Japanese: ミヤジマ  Miyajima ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He's one of the Trainers at the GR Water Fort . He will not duel against the player unless this uses a deck with only  Energy cards . When defeated, he gives out one Island of Fossil booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, he opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Senta .

title: Kanoko (TCG GB)
lore: Kanoko (Japanese: カノコ  Kanoko ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of GR Water Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . In all duels against her, the Mirage Place (Japanese: にげみずの 場  Place of Bitter Water ) rule is active. thus the Retreat cost of all Pokémon is one less than it would normally be. When defeated, she gives out two We Are Team Rocket booster packs and the GR Water Coin, also known as Psyduck Coin, which grants the player to enter GR Fighting Fort if the player also has the GR Fire Coin.

title: Shōko (TCG GB)
lore: Shōko (Japanese: ショウコ  Shōko ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is one of the Trainers at the GR Fire Fort . She will not duel against the player unless this uses a deck with four Eevee cards. When defeated, she gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and We Are Team Rocket booster packs. Also, when defeated for the first time, she frees Courtney and opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Hiderō , the Fort Leader of GR Fire Fort.

title: Yūki (TCG GB)
lore: Yūki (Japanese: ユウキ  Yūki ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is one of the Trainers at the GR Fire Fort . She refuses to battle the player unless they have only Energy in the active deck. When defeated, she gives out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, she opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Shōko .

title: Jes (TCG GB)
lore: Jes (Japanese: ジェス  Jes ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He is one of the Trainers at the GR Fire Fort . When defeated, he gives out one Island of Fossil booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, he opens the door to the next room so the player can reach Yūki .

title: Hiderō (TCG GB)
lore: Hiderō (Japanese: ヒデロウ  Hiderō ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of GR Fire Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . In all duels against him, the Flame Armor (Japanese: ほのおのよろい  Flame Armor ) rule is active, thus Pokémon's Weakness to is omitted. When defeated, he gives out one of both Team Rocket's Ambition and We Are Team Rocket booster packs and the GR Fire Coin, also known as Magmar Coin, which grants the player the ability to enter GR Fighting Fort if the player also has the GR Water Coin.

title: Ichikawa (TCG GB)
lore: Ichikawa (Japanese: イチカワ  Ichikawa ), also known as the Enigmatic Mask  GR3 (Japanese: GR3号  GR Number 3 ), is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . He has disguised himself behind a mask with a mark across it. In Pokémon Card GB 2, he has trapped the original members of the Water Club and Fire Club in small cages, and must be challenged in a 6-prize duel in order to free the Water Club crew. When defeated for the first time, the player is given one of both We Are Team Rocket and Island of Fossil booster packs. After being defeated at the Water Club, he moves to the Fire Club , where he may be challenged again in a 6-prize duel. When defeated there, he gives the two booster packs once again as well as one piece of the Team Great Rocket coin, and frees the Fire Club members. He appears again in the second room of the GR Lightning Fort . When the player meets him there for the first time, he reveals his identity. He can then be challenged to a duel, but only if the player's deck has only  Energy cards . He uses the This is the Power of Electricity Deck , and when defeated, he hands out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. He also releases the imprisoned Grand Master  Steve and opens the door to the next room, so the player can reach Catherine , the Fort Leader of the GB Lightning Fort.

title: Renna (TCG GB)
lore: Renna (Japanese: レンナ  Renna ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is one of the Trainers at the GR Lightning Fort . She accepts duels only if the player has 4 Pikachu cards in the active deck. Flying and Surfing Pikachu don't count. When defeated, she gives out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, she opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Ichikawa .

title: Catherine (TCG GB)
lore: Catherine (Japanese: キャサリン  Catherine ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of GR Lightning Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . In all duels against her, the Thunder Power Up (Japanese: 雷パワーアップ  Lightning Power Up ) rule is active, thus all Pokémon do 10 additional damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance) . When defeated, she gives out two We Are Team Rocket booster packs and the GR Lightning Coin, also known as Magnemite Coin, which grants the player to enter GR Fire Fort and GR Water Fort .

title: Miyuki (TCG GB)
lore:
Miyuki (Japanese: ミユキ  Miyuki ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is one of the Trainers at the GR Grass Fort . She refuses to duel against the player unless there are only  Energy cards in the active deck.
When defeated, she gives out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, she opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Morino , the Fort Leader of GR Grass Fort.

title: Yūta (TCG GB)
lore: Yūta (Japanese: ユウタ  Yūta ), also known as the Enigmatic Mask  GR1 (Japanese: GR1号  GR Number 1 ), is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Like a couple other Team Great Rocket members, he has disguised himself behind a mask with a pattern across it. He first appears at the Rock Club , from which he flees after the player arrives there, as Gene had given GR1 a rather sound beating, thus defending his crew and his club from Team Great Rocket's clutches. He then takes control over the Fighting Club , where he may be challenged in a 6-prize duel after Gene is defeated at the Rock Club. After defeating him, the player is awarded with one of both We Are Team Rocket and Beginning Pokémon booster packs and one piece of the Team Great Rocket Coin. He can be met again in the second room of the GR Grass Fort . When he's met for the first time, he reveals his identity. When defeated, he gives out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, he opens the door to the next room, allowing the player to reach Miyuki .

title: Midori (TCG GB)
lore: Midori (Japanese: ミドリ  Midori ) is a member of Team Great Rocket from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . She is one of the Trainers at the GR Grass Fort . When defeated, she gives out one We Are Team Rocket booster pack. Also, when defeated for the first time, she frees Rick , the Club Master of Science Club , from his prison, also allowing the player to advance to the next room, in which Yūta is.

title: Morino (TCG GB)
lore: Morino (Japanese: モリノ  Morino ) is a member of Team Great Rocket and the Fort Leader of GR Grass Fort from Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . In all duels against him, the Green Power (Japanese: みどりのちから  Green Power ) rule is active, thus no Pokémon can be inflicted with any Special Conditions . When defeated, he gives out two We Are Team Rocket booster packs and the GR Grass Coin, also known as Golbat Coin, which grants the player to enter GR Lightning Fort .

title: Mint (TCG GB)
lore: (Japanese: ミント  Mint ) is the female player character in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! . Her male counterpart is Mark and her rival is Ronald .

title: Master (Dragon Tamer clan)
lore: The Master (Japanese: 長老 さま  Master ) is the leader of the Dragon Tamer clan, a secret society of Dragon Tamers that worships Dragon-type Pokémon. He lives in the Dragon's Den , which is located north of Blackthorn City in Johto . In the English release of Pokémon Crystal , he is the leader of the dragon-user clan. In Pokémon Adventures , he is known as the Dragon Clan Elder .

title: Buena
lore: Buena (Japanese: アオイ  Aoi ) is the host of Buena's Password Show , an independent radio broadcast introduced in Pokémon Crystal , which becomes part of the Variety Channel in HeartGold and SoulSilver . In Generation II , this radio show is only broadcast at night until midnight , and in Generation IV , the show is broadcast every three hours between 2 AM and 11 PM. The player must remember the daily password to earn a point.

title: Eusine
lore: Eusine (Japanese: ミナキ  Minaki ; Eugene in The Legend of Thunder! ) is a character introduced in Pokémon Crystal . He is a researcher and expert on the Legendary beasts who has chased Suicune to no avail for ten years.

title: Kris (game)
lore: Kris (Japanese: クリス  Crys ) is the female playable character in Pokémon Crystal . Her male counterpart is Ethan . She does not appear in any other core series game; in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver , she is replaced by Lyra . She was the first female player character in the core series games , a feature that would be carried on in subsequent games.

title: Wilton
lore: Wilton (Japanese: ヒデノリ  Hidenori ) is a Fisherman and one of the few ordinary Trainers from the games to have also appeared in other media.

title: Li
lore: Li (Japanese: コウセイ  Kōsei ) is a Pokémon Trainer who first appeared in Pokémon Gold and Silver . He is the Elder of the Sprout Tower  Sages . He is an elderly man whose attire consists of a large purple robe covering most of his body, with a yellow robe over his right shoulder with a Poké Ball pattern. He bears a resemblance to Buddhist monks in real-world Japan. He is the only character in the games to have the Trainer class  Elder (Japanese: ちょうろう  Elder ). The title of Elder existed in Pokémon Gold, Silver , and Crystal but was not officially a Trainer class until Generation IV . Instead, it served as an honorific title that Sages used when referring to Li. Before the introduction of the class, Li simply belonged to the Sage class.

title: Mom (Johto)
lore: Mother or Mom (Japanese: おかあさん  mother ) is the mother of Ethan , Kris C , or Lyra HG SS .

title: Radio Director
lore: The Director (Japanese: きょくちょう  Director ) is the head of the Radio Tower in Goldenrod City . He appears in Pokémon Gold, Silver , Crystal , HeartGold, and SoulSilver .

title: Move Deleter
lore: A Move Deleter (Japanese: わすれオヤジ  Forgetful Man ) is a person who, for no charge, will make a Pokémon forget a move it knows. They are the counterparts to the Move Reminder , often found in the same location. Move Deleters appear in all core series games from Pokémon Gold and Silver up to Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon , as well as in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl , Pokémon Colosseum , and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness . All of the Move Deleters, excluding the one in Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, are characteristically forgetful (some even temporarily forgetting who they are). In Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! , no characters make Pokémon forget their moves. However, in these games, a forgetful man named Mr. Dazzling who used to live in the same house as the Move Deleter from Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen moves to a house on Route 12 and gives the player  TM32 ( Dazzling Gleam ). In Pokémon Sword and Shield , there is no traditional Move Deleter; instead, Jack offers to make Pokémon forget moves (among other services). In Pokémon Legends: Arceus , Scarlet, and Violet , there is no Move Deleter character at all, as it is possible to have Pokémon forget moves at any time outside of battle.

title: Maizie
lore: Maizie (Japanese: チエ  Chie ) is the granddaughter of Kurt , who lives with him in Azalea Town in Johto . She appears in the games , animation , and the Pokémon Adventures manga.

title: Kimono Girl
lore: A Kimono Girl (Japanese: まいこはん  Dancing Girl ) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that first appeared in the Generation II games. They appear as young women dressed in kimonos . Kimono Girls usually appear as a quintet of Trainers who each own one of Eevee 's Evolutions .

title: Kanto Pokémon Federation
lore: The Kanto Pokémon Federation (Japanese: カントーポケモンれんごう  Kanto Pokémon Federation ) is a Trainer group composed of Bikers (and a Cue Ball in FireRed and LeafGreen ) from Kanto .

title: Joey
lore: Joey (Japanese: ゴロウ  Gorō ) is a Youngster and one of the few regular Trainers from the games who also appears in other media.

title: Dude
lore: Dude (Japanese: おにいさん  Dude ) is a Trainer on Route 29 right outside New Bark Town in Pokémon Gold, Silver , and Crystal . He notices the player pass by a few times and decides to teach them how to catch Pokémon . He is the Generation II equivalent of the old man and was replaced with Lyra or Ethan in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver .

title: Kiyo
lore: Kiyo (Japanese: ノブヒコ  Nobuhiko ) is a Black Belt and the leader of the Fighting Dojo in Pokémon Gold, Silver , Crystal , HeartGold, and SoulSilver . He is known as the Karate King (Japanese: カラテだいおう  Great Karate King ).

title: Amphy
lore: Amphy (Japanese: アカリちゃん  Akari-chan ) is an Ampharos that illuminates the Olivine Lighthouse in Olivine City . Its Trainer is apparently Jasmine ; however, it does not appear to be an active member of her party . It has also made appearances in the animation and manga .

title: Carrie (game)
lore: Carrie (Japanese: オクル  Okuru ) is a little girl who appears in the Generation II  games . She is a frequent visitor of the Goldenrod Department Store , and loves to use Mystery Gift with people, and when talked to, Mystery Gift will be unlocked. She appears in Pokémon Stadium 2 to Mystery Gift with the player through the Transfer Pak . As with any user of Mystery Gift, she will appear in Viridian City 's Trainer House if she was the last person the player used Mystery Gift with. Also, as with any character battled in the Trainer House, her sprite will appear as Ethan 's Gold and Silver sprite (including in Pokémon Crystal , which uses a different sprite for Ethan himself). She will use one of three teams of six Pokémon each. There is no set pattern to which team she will use.

title: Webster (Johto)
lore: Webster (Japanese: ユウジ  Yūji ), known as Randy in Generation II , is a non-player character in Pokémon Gold, Silver , and Crystal as well as their remakes, HeartGold and SoulSilver . He is a guard posted at the gate between Goldenrod City and Route 35 . Webster gives the player his Spearow named Kenya (Japanese: ひきゃく  Hikyaku ) holding a mail , and asks them to deliver it to his friend on Route 31 . As a gesture of thanks, he will give the player an HP Up . Once the mail has been delivered, Webster's friend will hand out TM50 ( Nightmare ) in Generation II or TM44 ( Rest ) in Generation IV. It does not matter which Pokémon is given to Webster's friend, just that the mail is delivered. In Generation II, if the player removes the mail from Kenya, putting it in their PC , then gives the mail to another Pokémon, Webster's friend will take the mail and Pokémon from them. In Generation IV, however, any Pokémon replacing Kenya will be returned to the player. Due to this, a player may keep Kenya for the duration of the game or deliver it after evolving it into Fearow and still receive the TM . In the game, Webster is recognized as an in-game trader . However, Kenya is simply given to the player and no Pokémon sent to Webster in return. Unlike most Pokémon given by NPCs, Kenya has Webster's ID and OT , possibly because the player was meant to give the Spearow to Webster's friend. Hence, when battling with it, it will act like an outsider and receive the experience boost for traded Pokémon.

title: Cal (game)
lore: Cal (Japanese, Generation II: ヒカル  Hikaru , Generation IV: ひかる  Hikaru ) is a traveling Pokémon Trainer . He first appeared in Pokémon Gold and Silver , in which he was a Trainer that could be battled in Viridian City 's Trainer House . His sprite is the same as the sprite used for Ethan in Pokémon Gold and Silver ; this also applies to Pokémon Crystal , despite the fact that it introduced a new sprite for Ethan himself. He only appears in the Trainer House if the player has never used Mystery Gift before. If the player has used Mystery Gift, he is replaced with a Trainer with the same name and party of the last person the player used Mystery Gift with. His Pokémon are the fully evolved Johto first partner Pokémon at level 50. The three games also hold unused Trainer data for Cal, with one team consisting of the three unevolved first partner Pokémon at level 10, and the second forms of the first partner Pokémon at level 30. He also appeared in Pokémon Stadium 2 with a new unique character design as the opponent in the standard battle modes. He appears in the Battle Now and Free Battle modes as a CPU opponent. In Battle Now, he has access to the same Pokémon pools the player does. In Free Battle, Cal uses a team of Pokémon the player assigns him, except in the case of battles under Challenge Cup rules, in which case Cal receives Pokémon randomly in the same way the player does. In Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver , Cal has been given the appearance of an Ace Trainer .

title: Kurt
lore: Kurt (Japanese: ガンテツ  Gantetsu ) is a Poké Ball smith who lives in Azalea Town . In addition to making his own custom Balls out of Apricorns , he studies Poké Ball mechanics, and is known far and wide as a Poké Ball expert. He is Maizie 's grandfather.

title: Week Siblings
lore: The Week Siblings (Japanese: 曜日兄弟 ( ようびきょうだい )  Day-of-the-week Siblings ), also known as the Day-of-the-week Siblings , are seven characters from the Generation II and Generation IV games, Pokémon Gold, Silver , Crystal , HeartGold, and SoulSilver . Each of them appears at a certain location depending on the day of the week . They were one of the original aspects of the game to take advantage of the built-in clock system. The Zephyr Badge must be obtained for the siblings to appear.

title: DJ
lore: A DJ (Japanese: DJ  DJ ) is a person who presents a radio show in the Pokémon world .

title: DJ Mary
lore: DJ Mary (Japanese: クルミ  Kurumi ) is a DJ in Goldenrod Radio Tower . She co-hosts the famous radio program, Professor Oak's Pokémon Talk , with Professor Oak .

title: Earl Dervish
lore: Earl Dervish (Japanese: ジョバンニ  Giovanni ) is the teacher of Earl's Pokémon Academy (known as simply Pokémon School in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver ), located in Violet City in Pokémon Gold, Silver , Crystal , HeartGold, and SoulSilver, and in White City in Pokémon Stadium 2 .

title: Proton
lore: Proton (Japanese: ランス  Lance ) is one of the Team Rocket  Executives introduced in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . In Generation II , Proton's role was filled by two separate characters: an ordinary Grunt in the Slowpoke Well and an unnamed Executive in the Goldenrod Radio Tower .

title: Petrel
lore: Petrel (Japanese: ラムダ  Lambda ) is one of the Team Rocket  Executives introduced in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver . In Generation II , Petrel's role was filled by two separate unnamed Executives: one in the Team Rocket HQ and another in the Goldenrod Radio Tower disguised as the Director.

title: Ariana
lore: Ariana (Japanese: アテナ  Athena ) is one of the Team Rocket  Executives introduced in Pokémon Gold and Silver . She was not given an official name until Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver .

title: Archer
